Drag and drop blocks into the Configuration Rules canvas to create logical rules, then apply them to the set of configurations.

controls.name: User Coordinate System (UCS)
controls.tooltip:
Creates a custom coordinate system that you can reference in assembly relationships, manufacturing setups or other downstream workflows.

Select a Snap point on a component to place the coordinate system. Optionally, adjust its position, orientation, and axis alignment.

controls.name: Offset Plane
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Plane that is offset from the selected face or plane.

Select a face, plane or sketch profile, then specify the offset distance.

controls.name: Plane at Angle
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Plane through an edge, axis, or line at a specific angle.

Select a linear edge, axis, or sketch line to position the plane, then specify the rotation angle.

controls.name: Tangent Plane
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Plane that is tangent to a face.

Select a face to create a plane tangent to, then select a reference point or face or plane (when cylindrical face is selected) to align to or adjust the angle to rotate the plane around face.

controls.name: Midplane
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Plane at the midpoint between two faces or planes.

Select two faces or planes to create a Construction Plane between them.

controls.name: Perpendicular Plane
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Plane that is perpendicular to a plane or face.

Select a plane or face to create a construction plane that is perpendicular to the plane or face. Optionally, select a point or face to refine location.

controls.name: Plane Through Two Edges
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Plane that passes through two edges or axes.

Select two linear edges, axes or sketch lines to create a Construction Plane through.

controls.name: Plane Through Three Points
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Plane that passes through three points or vertices.

Select three points or vertices to create a Construction Plane through.

controls.name: Plane Along Path
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Plane normal to an edge or sketch line.

Select an edge or sketch line to create a Construction Plane along.

controls.name: Axis Through Cylinder/Cone/Torus
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Axis through the center of a cylinder, cone or torus.

Select a cylinder, cone, or torus to create an axis through its center.

controls.name: Axis Perpendicular To Face
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Axis that is perpendicular to a face and passes through a specific point.

Select a face or plane and a vertex or sketch point to create an axis that is perpendicular to the plane and coincident with the point.

controls.name: Axis Through Two Planes
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Axis coincident with the intersection of two faces or planes.

Select two faces or planes to create an axis where they intersect.

controls.name: Axis Through Two Points
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Axis that passes through two points or vertices.

Select two vertices or sketch points to create a Construction Axis that is coincident with both vertices and points.

controls.name: Axis Through Edge
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Axis along a linear edge or sketch curve.

Select a linear edge, axis or sketch line to place the axis.

controls.name: Point At Vertex
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Point at an existing point or vertex.

Select a vertex or sketch point to place the Construction Point.

controls.name: Point Through Two Edges
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Point at the intersection or extended intersection of two edges.

Select two edges or sketch lines to create a Construction Point where they intersect.

controls.name: Point Through Three Planes
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Point at the intersection or extended intersection of three non-parallel planes or faces.

Select three planes, faces, or sketch profiles to create a Construction Point where they intersect.

controls.name: Point At Center Of Circle/Sphere/Torus
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Point at the center of a circle, sphere, or torus.

Select a circular face or sketch profile, spherical face, or toroidal face to create a Construction Point at its center.

controls.name: Point At Edge And Plane
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Point at the intersection of a linear edge, sketch line, or axis with a face or plane.

Select a linear edge, sketch line, or axis and a face or plane to create a Construction Point where they intersect.

controls.name: Point Along Path
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Point at a specific distance along the path.

Select an edge, sketch line, or curve to use as the path to create the Construction Point along. Optionally, specify a distance to place the point.

controls.name: Measure
controls.tooltip:
Measures the distance, angle, area, or position of selected objects.

Select an object to measure it, and optionally select a second object to measure it and the distance between them.

controls.name: Interference
controls.tooltip:
Reports the interference between selected solid bodies or components.

Select the components then click compute. Choose to create components from the interferences.

controls.name: Section Analysis
controls.tooltip:
Creates a view that cuts through all visible objects in a design to reveal interior details and obscured features.

Select a planar object to define the cut plane, then adjust the distance and angles to position it in the design. In the Browser, the Section Analysis displays in the Analysis folder, where you can adjust its visibility, edit it, or delete it.

controls.name: Curvature Comb Analysis
controls.tooltip:
Displays a comb with sample points along selected edges of a body to help you analyze the curvature of a surface.

Select edges to analyze on a body, then adjust the density and scale of the curvature comb.

controls.name: Curvature Map Analysis
controls.tooltip:
Displays a color gradient on bodies to help you analyze areas of high and low surface curvature.

controls.name: Zebra Analysis

controls.name: Accessibility Analysis

controls.name: Center of Mass
controls.tooltip:
Displays a center mark glyph at the center of mass for the selected objects.

You can measure from the center mark to other objects.

controls.name: Minimum Radius Analysis
controls.tooltip:

controls.name: DOF Analysis
controls.tooltip: Displays Degree of Freedom of each component in the Assembly.

controls.name: Fastener Stack Analysis

controls.name: Find Similar Components

controls.name: Navigator

controls.name: History

controls.name: Select

controls.name: Window Selection
controls.tooltip:

Use Selection Filters to include or exclude objects by type.

controls.name: Freeform Selection
controls.tooltip:
Selects objects enclosed in an irregular (lasso) selection area.

A clockwise boundary shape selects all objects within the boundary. A counterclockwise boundary shape selects all visible objects crossed by the boundary.

Use Selection Filters to include or exclude objects by type.

controls.name: Paint Selection
controls.tooltip:
Press and hold the left mouse button and move across objects to select them.

Use Selection Filters to include or exclude objects by type.

children.name: Select By Name

Enter a portion of the object name, check the object types to include, then click Find. You can search using one or more characters or words, finding only objects having that string in the name.

children.name: Select By Boundary
children.tooltip:
Selects objects using a boundary shape you choose.

Select a body to set the centroid, boundary shape, Selection Type, and whether intersected objects are selected.

children.name: Select By Size
children.tooltip:
Selects bodies or components within a size range that you specify.

Use the slider controls or specify the minimum and maximum size values. The size value is the distance between the opposing diagonal corners of the body or component bounding box.

children.name: Invert Selection
children.tooltip:
Switches the selection state of all objects.

Selection is based on the active selection filter and selection mode.

children.name: Seed And Boundary

Select faces or edges on a solid or surface body to define the selection boundary, then select a face on the body to use as the seed object for the selection set. Click Update to refresh the selection set based on the current boundary and seed objects.

controls.name: Component Drag
controls.tooltip:
Enables or disables the movement of components by dragging in the canvas.

Hold Alt to drag components when Component Drag is disabled.

children.name: Select Body Priority
children.tooltip:
Sets the selection filter to Bodies, and prevents selection of other object types.

Click a body to select it. Hold Ctrl (Windows) or Command (MacOS) to add objects to or remove objects from the selection. Click Select Body Priority again to restore selection of any object type.

children.name: Select Face Priority
children.tooltip:
Sets the selection filter to Body Faces, and prevents selection of other object types.

Click a face to select it. Hold Ctrl (Windows) or Command (MacOS) to add objects to or remove objects from the selection. Click Select Face Priority again to restore selection of any object type.

children.name: Select Edge Priority
children.tooltip:

Click an edge on a body to select it. Hold Ctrl (Windows) or Command (MacOS) to add objects to or remove objects from the selection. Click Select Edge Priority again to restore selection of any object type.

children.name: Select Component Priority
children.tooltip:
Sets the selection filter to Components, and prevents selection of other object types.

Click a component to select it. Hold Ctrl (Windows) or Command (MacOS) to add objects to or remove objects from the selection. Click Select Component Priority again to restore selection of any object type.

controls.name: Selection Filters
controls.tooltip:
Specifies which object types can be selected.

Use Select All to include or exclude all object types. Check only specific types to limit selection to those types. Check Select Through to enable selection of hidden objects during Window or Freeform selection.

controls.name: Capture Position
controls.tooltip:
Captures the positions of recently moved/rotated components as an event in your timeline. This information is used by geometry and assemble commands.

Use this if you intend to continue modeling/assembling while keeping components at their current positions.

controls.name: Revert Position
controls.tooltip: Returns the components to the previous position and rotation.

controls.name: Assign Item Number
controls.tooltip:
Assign unique item numbers to selected components for tracking throughout their life cycles.

Items are set to “unreleased” and are accessible in Fusion Manage.

controls.name: Quick Release
controls.tooltip:
Transitions the component to the next life cycle state or revision without a change order.

The final release still requires a change order. This only works on the top level component or external references - not internal components.

controls.name: Release with Change Order
controls.tooltip:
Releases the selected components with a change order.

Includes full audit trail and approval workflow. Internal components and external references are supported.

controls.name: Bill of Materials
controls.tooltip:
Opens the bill of materials for this design.

(May not be available in some situations, such as when viewing a configured design, or when Fusion is offline.)

controls.name: Dashboard
controls.tooltip:
Opens the Fusion Manage Dashboard in your default browser.

The Dashboard is a central place where you can access your Fusion Manage information, such as charts and outstanding work.

controls.name: Details
controls.tooltip:
Opens Fusion Manage in your default browser and shows the Details page for the currently selected item.

If the current selection is not assigned as an item in Fusion Manage, the list of items and BOMs is shown.

controls.name: Change Orders
controls.tooltip:
Opens Fusion Manage in your default browser and shows change order information for the currently selected item.

If the current selection is not assigned as an item in Fusion Manage, the list of change orders is shown.

controls.name: Open tasks in web
controls.tooltip:
Opens all tasks in your default web browser.

View and manage all your assigned tasks in the web interface.

controls.name: Create new task
controls.tooltip:
Creates a new task in the task management system.

Opens a dialog to create and assign a new task.

controls.name: Related tasks
controls.tooltip:
Shows tasks related to the current item or selection.

View and manage tasks that are associated with the current context.

Prepares solid or mesh bodies to be 3D printed directly from Fusion's Manufacture workspace or from an external application.

Select solid or mesh bodies to prepare, then select a Preparation Type to switch to the Manufacture workspace, export and send to an installed 3D printing application, or export a 3MF, STL, or OBJ file. For exports, adjust the output and refinement settings to control the resolution of the mesh.

Displays the Scripts and Add-Ins dialog box. Create, edit, run, stop, debug and manage Scripts and Add-Ins.

Navigate between libraries, create new libraries, and add physical materials or appearances to your Favorites. In custom libraries, edit the properties of physical materials and appearances, or create new ones.

controls.tooltip:
Computes all of the parameters, features, and assembly relationships in a design.

Use at major milestones in the design process and after making significant changes to features in the Timeline, to ensure all assembly relationships are calculated properly.

controls.name: Measure

Select an object to measure it, and optionally select a second object to measure it and the distance between them.

controls.name: Interference

Select the components then click compute. Choose to create components from the interferences.

controls.name: Create Unlinked PCB
controls.tooltip:
Creates a 3D PCB document from the selected sketch or face.

Select a sketch or face, then select origin and axes orientation. You can convert circles into non-plated through holes (NPTHs).

controls.name: PCB Profile
controls.tooltip:
Define the shape of the PCB via a sketched profile.

Select a profile and an origin point.

controls.name: Copy EAGLE Profile
controls.tooltip: Copies the profile supplied from EAGLE to an upstream Fusion sketch.

controls.name: Edit EAGLE Profile
controls.tooltip: Edit the sketch generated from EAGLE board.

controls.name: Move PCB Components
controls.tooltip:
Move PCB components to new locations on the board.

Select a component and move it by dragging or typing in values.

controls.name: PCB Status
controls.tooltip:
Check the status of the PCB shape and component positions.

Both the board shape and the component positions can be driven by either Fusion or EAGLE. Use this command to understand the state of the model.

controls.name: User Coordinate System (UCS)
controls.tooltip:
Creates a custom coordinate system that you can reference in assembly relationships, manufacturing setups or other downstream workflows.

Select a Snap point on a component to place the coordinate system. Optionally, adjust its position, orientation, and axis alignment.

controls.name: Offset Plane
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Plane that is offset from the selected face or plane.

Select a face, plane or sketch profile, then specify the offset distance.

controls.name: Plane at Angle
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Plane through an edge, axis, or line at a specific angle.

Select a linear edge, axis, or sketch line to position the plane, then specify the rotation angle.

controls.name: Tangent Plane
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Plane that is tangent to a face.

Select a face to create a plane tangent to, then select a reference point or face or plane (when cylindrical face is selected) to align to or adjust the angle to rotate the plane around face.

controls.name: Midplane
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Plane at the midpoint between two faces or planes.

Select two faces or planes to create a Construction Plane between them.

controls.name: Perpendicular Plane
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Plane that is perpendicular to a plane or face.

Select a plane or face to create a construction plane that is perpendicular to the plane or face. Optionally, select a point or face to refine location.

controls.name: Plane Through Two Edges
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Plane that passes through two edges or axes.

Select two linear edges, axes or sketch lines to create a Construction Plane through.

controls.name: Plane Through Three Points
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Plane that passes through three points or vertices.

Select three points or vertices to create a Construction Plane through.

controls.name: Plane Along Path
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Plane normal to an edge or sketch line.

Select an edge or sketch line to create a Construction Plane along.

controls.name: Axis Through Cylinder/Cone/Torus
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Axis through the center of a cylinder, cone or torus.

Select a cylinder, cone, or torus to create an axis through its center.

controls.name: Axis Perpendicular To Face
controls.tooltip:

Select a face or plane and a vertex or sketch point to create an axis that is perpendicular to the plane and coincident with the point.

controls.name: Axis Through Two Planes
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Axis coincident with the intersection of two faces or planes.

Select two faces or planes to create an axis where they intersect.

controls.name: Axis Through Two Points
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Axis that passes through two points or vertices.

Select two vertices or sketch points to create a Construction Axis that is coincident with both vertices and points.

controls.name: Axis Through Edge
controls.tooltip:

Select a linear edge, axis or sketch line to place the axis.

controls.name: Point At Vertex

Select a vertex or sketch point to place the Construction Point.

controls.name: Point Through Two Edges

Select two edges or sketch lines to create a Construction Point where they intersect.

controls.name: Point Through Three Planes

controls.name: Sustainability Insights
controls.tooltip:
Displays an estimated carbon footprint of the current design.

Select a body to analyze, then specify manufacturing details to improve your footprint estimate. You can also activate a persistent dock to monitor selected bodies as you work.

controls.name: Decal
controls.tooltip:
Places an image on a selected face as a cosmetic decal.

Select a PNG, JPG, or TIF image file from a Fusion project or your local computer. Select a face on a solid or surface body to apply it to, then adjust its orientation, scale, and opacity.

controls.name: Canvas
controls.tooltip:
Places an image on a planar face or sketch plane.

Select a face then select an image to import.

controls.name: Insert T-Spline
controls.tooltip:
Inserts a T-Spline Mesh (TSM) file as a single T-Spline body or a T-Spline Scene (TSS) file as one or more T-Spline bodies.

Select the TSM or TSS file you want to insert, then click Open. The T-Spline bodies display in the canvas and Browser and you can use the Form tools to edit them.

controls.name: Insert SVG
controls.tooltip:
Imports an SVG file into the active sketch.

Use SVG files for vector artwork such as logos or custom text.

controls.name: Insert DXF
controls.tooltip:
Inserts geometry from a DXF file into the active sketch.

Select a face or plane, select the DXF file to insert, then position the geometry on the plane.

Select the unit type that matches the units from the original design that generated the DXF.

controls.name: Insert Mesh
controls.tooltip:
Inserts an existing STL, OBJ, or 3MF file as a mesh body into the active component in a design.

Select a file to insert. The contents of the file displays as a mesh body in the canvas and the browser.

For STL or OBJ files, select the unit type that matches the units from the original design that generated the STL or OBJ.

controls.name: Insert Component
controls.tooltip:
Inserts the selected component into the current design.

Select the component to insert then use the manipulator to adjust the position.

controls.name: Insert Fastener
controls.tooltip:
Inserts a fastener into the active document.

Use a combination of searching, filtering and browsing to locate a fastener, adjust the settings, and select a geometry (an edge, a face, a sketch point, an existing fastener) or place a fastener anywhere in the canvas to position it.

controls.name: Duplicate With Joints
controls.tooltip:
Duplicates components in an assembly and the joints attached to them.

Select components to duplicate, select a Joint Origin Mode, then select a Snap point to place each instance. If a component has multiple joints, select the next row in the selection box, then select a Snap point to place each instance.

controls.name: Insert Derive
controls.tooltip:
Pulls and links design features from another design into the active design. When you update the derived features in the original design, the changes are reflected in the destination design.

Before you start, activate the component that you want to contain the derived design features. Select a design, then select a set of components, bodies, sketches, construction geometry, flat patterns, or parameters to derive into the current design.

controls.name: Insert McMaster-Carr Component
controls.tooltip:
Insert a McMaster-Carr Component into the active document.

Browse to the desired component, click the Product Detail CAD icon, select the file type, then click Save.

controls.name: Insert a manufacturer part
controls.tooltip: parts4cad lets you browse and configure millions of parts from more than 400 supplier and manufacturer catalogs and insert them into your designs.

controls.name: Insert TraceParts Supplier Components
controls.tooltip: With TraceParts, boost your design productivity and access millions of CAD models from hundreds of supplier catalogs.

controls.name: Add To Assembly
controls.tooltip:
Inserts the active design into an Assembly Design as an external component.

Select an Assembly Design to insert into, then use the manipulators in the canvas or Initial Position dialog to place the component in the target design.

controls.name: Select
controls.tooltip:
Selection is always active and the active selection mode displays here.

Hold Ctrl (Windows) or Command (MacOS) to add objects to or remove objects from the selection. Change the active selection mode by selecting the mode you want to work with from the menu. Use the selection mode and selection filters to fine tune selection.

controls.name: Window Selection
controls.tooltip:
Selects objects enclosed in a rectangular selection area.

Click and drag from left to right (window selection) to select objects enclosed by the selection boundary. Click and drag from right to left (crossing selection) to select all visible objects the selection boundary intersects and encloses.

Use Selection Filters to include or exclude objects by type.

controls.name: Freeform Selection
controls.tooltip:
Selects objects enclosed in an irregular (lasso) selection area.

A clockwise boundary shape selects all objects within the boundary. A counterclockwise boundary shape selects all visible objects crossed by the boundary.

Use Selection Filters to include or exclude objects by type.

controls.name: Paint Selection
controls.tooltip:
Press and hold the left mouse button and move across objects to select them.

Use Selection Filters to include or exclude objects by type.

children.name: Select By Name
children.tooltip:
Selects bodies or components by the name used in the Browser.

Enter a portion of the object name, check the object types to include, then click Find. You can search using one or more characters or words, finding only objects having that string in the name.

children.name: Select By Boundary
children.tooltip:
Selects objects using a boundary shape you choose.

Select a body to set the centroid, boundary shape, Selection Type, and whether intersected objects are selected.

children.name: Select By Size
children.tooltip:
Selects bodies or components within a size range that you specify.

Use the slider controls or specify the minimum and maximum size values. The size value is the distance between the opposing diagonal corners of the body or component bounding box.

children.name: Invert Selection
children.tooltip:
Switches the selection state of all objects.

Selection is based on the active selection filter and selection mode.

children.name: Seed And Boundary
children.tooltip:
Automatically creates a selection set that includes faces on a solid or surface body that are located between a set of boundary objects and a seed object.

Select faces or edges on a solid or surface body to define the selection boundary, then select a face on the body to use as the seed object for the selection set. Click Update to refresh the selection set based on the current boundary and seed objects.

controls.name: Component Drag
controls.tooltip:
Enables or disables the movement of components by dragging in the canvas.

Hold Alt to drag components when Component Drag is disabled.

children.name: Select Body Priority
children.tooltip:
Sets the selection filter to Bodies, and prevents selection of other object types.

Click a body to select it. Hold Ctrl (Windows) or Command (MacOS) to add objects to or remove objects from the selection. Click Select Body Priority again to restore selection of any object type.

children.name: Select Face Priority
children.tooltip:
Sets the selection filter to Body Faces, and prevents selection of other object types.

Click a face to select it. Hold Ctrl (Windows) or Command (MacOS) to add objects to or remove objects from the selection. Click Select Face Priority again to restore selection of any object type.

children.name: Select Edge Priority
children.tooltip:
Sets the selection filter to Body Edges, and prevents selection of other object types.

Click an edge on a body to select it. Hold Ctrl (Windows) or Command (MacOS) to add objects to or remove objects from the selection. Click Select Edge Priority again to restore selection of any object type.

children.name: Select Component Priority
children.tooltip:
Sets the selection filter to Components, and prevents selection of other object types.

Click a component to select it. Hold Ctrl (Windows) or Command (MacOS) to add objects to or remove objects from the selection. Click Select Component Priority again to restore selection of any object type.

controls.name: Selection Filters
controls.tooltip:
Specifies which object types can be selected.

Use Select All to include or exclude all object types. Check only specific types to limit selection to those types. Check Select Through to enable selection of hidden objects during Window or Freeform selection.

controls.name: Finish PCB
controls.tooltip: Return to the Model workspace.

controls.name: Move/Copy
controls.tooltip:
Moves the selected face, body, sketch, or construction geometry a specified distance or angle.

Select the objects to modify then specify the distance or angle. Use Set Pivot to reposition the manipulator.

controls.name: Measure
controls.tooltip:
Measures the distance, angle, area, or position of selected objects.

Select an object to measure it, and optionally select a second object to measure it and the distance between them.

controls.name: Create Sketch
controls.tooltip:
Enters Sketch mode, where you create geometric profiles that define the foundation of a design. Then use commands like Extrude, Revolve, and Loft to create 3D bodies from sketches.

Select a construction plane, then create lines, arcs, or points to create sketch and construction geometry. Constrain sketches with dimensions and constraints. Select Finish Sketch to exit Sketch mode.

controls.name: Create Form
controls.tooltip:
Enters Form mode and inserts a form feature into the timeline. Use form tools to create and edit history-free bodies by pushing and pulling on vertices, edges, and faces. This is commonly referred to as T-Spline modeling.

Select Finish Form to exit out of the mode.

controls.name: Derive
controls.tooltip:
Pushes and links design features from the active design into a new or existing design. When you update the derived features in the original design, the changes are reflected in the destination design.

Select a single component or a set of components, bodies, sketches, construction geometry, flat patterns, or parameters to derive from the active design.

controls.name: Automated Modeling
controls.tooltip:
Generates design alternatives between geometries in space that you want to connect.

Select at least two faces to connect. Optionally, you can select areas where you don't want to create new geometry. The alternatives are generated automatically. Explore them and select the alternative that best suits your needs.

controls.name: Extrude
controls.tooltip:
Adds depth to open or closed sketch profiles or faces.

Select an extrusion type, select sketch profiles or faces to extrude, then specify the distance and taper angle. For the Thin Extrude type, specify the wall thickness.

controls.name: Revolve
controls.tooltip:
Revolves a sketch profile or planar face around a selected axis.

Select a profile or planar face and an axis to revolve around, then specify the extent type, direction, and operation.

controls.name: Sweep
controls.tooltip:
Sweeps a sketch profile, planar face, or a solid body along a selected path.

Select a sweep type, an object and a path to sweep along, then specify the operation. Optionally select rails or a centerline to guide the sweep.

controls.name: Loft
controls.tooltip:
Creates a transitional shape between two or more sketch profiles or planar faces.

Select a series of profiles or planar faces to define a shape. Optionally select rails or a centerline to guide the shape.

controls.name: Rib
controls.tooltip:
Creates a thin feature from an open sketch profile, extruded to the nearest faces on a solid body. The rib feature is extruded in a direction parallel to the sketch plane.

Select an open sketch profile, then specify the thickness.

controls.name: Web
controls.tooltip:
Creates a thin feature from an open sketch profile, extruded to the nearest faces on a solid body. The web feature is extruded in a direction perpendicular to the sketch plane.

Select an open sketch profile, then specify the thickness.

controls.name: Emboss
controls.tooltip:
Raises or recesses a sketch profile relative to faces on a solid body by a specified depth and direction.

Select sketch profiles, select faces on a solid body to emboss, then adjust depth, effect, and alignment.

controls.name: Hole
controls.tooltip:
Creates a hole based on user-specified values and selections.

Select a face to place the hole then select edges to position the hole on the face, or select sketch points to place multiple holes. Specify the hole type, tap type and size values.

controls.name: Thread
controls.tooltip:
Add internal or external threads to cylindrical geometry. Threads can be cosmetic or modeled on the geometry.

Select a cylindrical face then set the thread specifications.

controls.name: Box
controls.tooltip:
Creates a solid box.

Select a plane, draw a rectangle then specify the height of the box.

controls.name: Cylinder
controls.tooltip:
Creates a solid cylinder.

Select a plane, draw a circle then specify the height of the cylinder.

controls.name: Sphere
controls.tooltip:
Creates a solid body sphere.

Select a plane then specify the center point of the sphere and the diameter.

controls.name: Torus
controls.tooltip:
Creates a solid torus.

Specify the center point and diameter of the axis of revolution of the torus.

controls.name: Coil
controls.tooltip:
Creates a solid coil.

Select a plane then draw a circle to specify the major diameter of the coil. Finish defining the coil using the manipulators or dialog box.

controls.name: Pipe
controls.tooltip:
Creates a solid pipe that follows a selected path.

Select the path then specify the section and size.

controls.name: Bounding Solid
controls.tooltip:
Creates a solid component around a selected component, body, or set of bodies.

Select objects to be enclosed and adjust the shape and size or offset parameters as needed. The resulting bounding solid is a standalone component that can be used for measurements, serve as a reference for the stock volume for manufacturing, or as a base for an outer shell design.

children.name: Rectangular Pattern
children.tooltip:
Duplicates faces, bodies, features, or components in a design and distributes them along linear axes in rows and columns to create a rectangular pattern.

Select the object type, then select objects to pattern in the canvas, Browser, or Timeline. Select one or more axes to distribute the pattern instances along, then adjust distribution, quantity, and distance. Check Suppression, then uncheck instances in the canvas to remove them from the pattern.

children.name: Circular Pattern
children.tooltip:
Duplicates faces, bodies, features, or components in a design and distributes them around a linear axis to create a circular pattern.

Select the object type, then select objects to pattern in the canvas, Browser, or Timeline. Select the axis to distribute the pattern instances around, then adjust distribution, quantity, and distance. Check Suppression, then uncheck instances in the canvas to remove them from the pattern.

children.name: Pattern on Path
children.tooltip:
Duplicates faces, bodies, features, or components in a design and distributes them to create a pattern along a specific path.

Select the object type, then select objects to pattern in the canvas, Browser, or Timeline. Select the path to distribute the pattern instances along, then adjust distribution, quantity, and distance. Check Suppression, then uncheck instances in the canvas to remove them from the pattern.

children.name: Geometric Pattern
children.tooltip:
Creates a pattern with size and distribution gradients across a face on a solid body.

Select the face to pattern across, select a solid body as the object to pattern, then adjust the size and distribution settings.

controls.name: Mirror
controls.tooltip:
Creates a copy of selected faces, bodies, features, or components, mirrored across a plane.

Select the objects to mirror, then select the mirror plane.

controls.name: Thicken
controls.tooltip:
Adds thickness to surface faces to create a solid body.

Select the faces to thicken, then specify a thickness value.

controls.name: Boundary Fill
controls.tooltip:
Creates, joins or removes volumes using bounding volumes formed by tool selections.

Select solids, surfaces or workplanes as tools to form volumes (or cells). These cells can be used to cut existing solids or to join to existing solids or to create a new solid.

controls.name: Find Features
controls.tooltip:
Identifies features in a body. Recognized features are listed in the browser.

Select the bodies then specify the feature types to identify.

controls.name: Fluid Volume
controls.tooltip:
Creates the surrounding volume from selected bodies. Surrounding volume can be internal or external to the bodies. The surrounding volume is created in a new component.

Select solid bodies, capping surfaces, or work planes as tools to form the surrounding volume.

controls.name: Create Base Feature
controls.tooltip:
Enters direct editing mode and inserts a history-free feature in the timeline. Actions performed while in the Base Feature are not recorded in the timeline.

Select Finish Base Feature to exit out of the mode.

children.name: Create Linked PCB
children.tooltip:
Creates a new 3D PCB document as an external component in the assembly. If the board outline sketch references assembly geometry, the board updates with design changes.

Select location, then open the 3D PCB to complete a closed profile in the board outline to finish defining the board.

children.name: Derive PCB
children.tooltip:
Derives a new 3D PCB Document from a sketch profile. The derived profile replaces the board outline sketch. Updates to the derived features in the original design reflect in the destination design.

Select a sketch profile, then select the origin and axes orientation.

children.name: Create Unlinked PCB
children.tooltip:
Creates a 3D PCB document from the selected sketch or face.

Select a sketch or face, then select origin and axes orientation. You can convert circles into non-plated through holes (NPTHs).

controls.name: Joint Origin
controls.tooltip:
Positions a joint origin on a component. Joint origins define the geometry used to relate a joint's components.

Select geometry to define the joint origin.

controls.name: Generate Timeline
controls.tooltip:
AutoTimeline capabilities in this preview may evolve over time, and your feedback helps improve results.

AutoTimeline helps generate a parametric timeline for imported bodies, making them easier to edit and reuse in Fusion.

controls.name: Press Pull
controls.tooltip: Modifies the selected geometry using offset, extrude, or fillet commands. The operation depends on the geometry selected.

controls.name: Edit Face
controls.tooltip:
Converts the selected face to T-Spline faces, edges, and vertices for modification.

Select the face to modify. Increase the length and width factors to add faces to give more control.

controls.name: Fillet
controls.tooltip:
Rounds the edges of a solid body by adding material to interior edges and removing material from exterior edges.

Select edges, faces, or features, then specify a radius. Use the Rule Fillet type to add fillets based on specified rules. Use the Full Round Fillet type to round the edges over three adjacent faces.

controls.name: Chamfer
controls.tooltip:
Bevels the edges of a solid or surface body by removing material from exterior edges or adding material to interior edges.

Select edges, faces, or features, then specify one distance, two distances, or a distance and an angle.

controls.name: Shell
controls.tooltip:
Offsets the walls of a solid body to create a hollow cavity with walls of a specified thickness.

Select a body to shell or faces to remove to create an opening, then specify a type, direction, and wall thickness.

controls.name: Draft
controls.tooltip:
Applies a fixed or parting line draft angle to planar faces.

Select a pull direction, parting tool, and faces to draft, then specify the draft angle.

controls.name: Scale
controls.tooltip:
Scales sketch objects, bodies, or components.

Select the objects to scale then specify the scale factor.

controls.name: Combine
controls.tooltip:
Joins, cuts, or intersects two or more solid bodies to create a single solid body.

Select the target body, select one or more tool bodies to combine with the target body, then select the operation to use to combine the bodies together.

controls.name: Offset Face
controls.tooltip:
Shifts the selected face or faces in a positive or negative direction.

Select a single face or multiple faces and specify the Offset distance.

controls.name: Replace Face
controls.tooltip:
Replaces one or more part faces with different face. The new face must completely intersect the part.

Select the face to remove then select the new face.

controls.name: Split Face
controls.tooltip:
Divides faces using a selected profile, face, or plane as the cutting tool.

Select the faces to modify then select the profile, face, or plane that divides the source face.

controls.name: Split Body
controls.tooltip:
Creates new bodies by dividing selected bodies using a profile, face, or plane.

Select the bodies to modify then select the profile, face, or plane that divides the bodies.

controls.name: Silhouette Split
controls.tooltip:
Splits a body using surfaces generated from its silhouette curves.

Set the view direction by selecting a plane or axis then select the body and choose a split operation.

controls.name: Move/Copy
controls.tooltip:
Moves the selected face, body, sketch, or construction geometry a specified distance or angle.

Select the objects to modify then specify the distance or angle. Use Set Pivot to reposition the manipulator.

controls.name: Align
controls.tooltip:
Moves an object (component, body, sketch, work geometry) by aligning geometry selected from the object with geometry selected elsewhere. Geometry can be a point, line, plane, circle, or coordinate system. Snaps are treated as full coordinate systems for full position and orientation alignment.

Select the point on the object to move then select the point on the face to align to. Click Flip and Angle to rotate the object.

controls.name: Delete
controls.tooltip:
Permanently deletes selected objects, and everything related to them, from the design. Does not create a feature in the timeline. Deleted objects cannot be restored parametrically.

Select components, bodies, sketches, and construction objects to delete. Use the Remove command to preserve parametric history.

controls.name: Remove
controls.tooltip:
Deletes selected components or bodies from the design and preserves the operation as a feature in the timeline. Removed objects can be restored parametrically.

Select components or bodies to remove. To permanently delete parametric history associated with an object, use the Delete command instead.

controls.name: Arrange
controls.tooltip: Quickly arrange items on a plane or sketch for manufacturing.

children.name: Remove Features
children.tooltip:
Automatically deletes features from selected objects.

Select objects, from which to delete features, and choose appropriate settings. Associated features are selected and deleted accordingly.

children.name: Remove Faces
children.tooltip:
Deletes selected faces.

Select faces to remove. Neighboring faces are automatically deleted, as appropriate, in order to heal the model.

children.name: Replace with Primitives
children.tooltip:
Replaces selected objects with primitive shapes.

Choose appropriate objects and define the replacement shape. The default primitive shape bounds all selected objects and the original objects are suppressed.

controls.name: Volumetric Lattice
controls.tooltip: Create a new volumetric lattice using the selected geometry as the boundary of the volume.

controls.name: Volumetric Texture
controls.tooltip: Create a new volumetric texture using the selected geometry as the boundary of the volume.

controls.name: Physical Material
controls.tooltip:
Assigns physical materials to components and bodies in a design to control their thermal, mechanical, strength, and advanced engineering properties, as well as their appearance.

Drag physical materials onto components or bodies in the canvas or the Browser. In the In This Design section, right-click physical materials to edit, duplicate, delete, or add them as favorites.

controls.name: Appearance
controls.tooltip:
Assigns appearances to components, bodies, or faces in a design to override the color and texture of their physical materials, without affecting physical engineering properties.

Choose whether to apply appearances to components and bodies or specific faces, then drag appearances onto components, bodies, or faces in the canvas or the Browser. In the In This Design section, right-click appearances to edit, duplicate, delete, or add them as favorites.

controls.name: Manage Materials
controls.tooltip:
Opens the Material Browser, where you can manage physical materials and appearances in user-defined material libraries.

Navigate between libraries, create new libraries, and add physical materials or appearances to your Favorites. In custom libraries, edit the properties of physical materials and appearances, or create new ones.

controls.name: Change Parameters
controls.tooltip:
Displays the Parameters dialog, where you can create and manage equations and relationships to control the size of objects.

Edit the name, expression, and comments for parameters. Create User Parameters to use in other expressions.

controls.name: Compute All
controls.tooltip:
Computes all of the parameters, features, and assembly relationships in a design.

Use at major milestones in the design process and after making significant changes to features in the Timeline, to ensure all assembly relationships are calculated properly.

controls.name: Compute Unresolved
controls.tooltip:
Computes only the features related to unresolved external components in the assembly.

Only available when you open a design that contains unresolved external components. You must compute the features related to the unresolved components before you can edit or save the design.

controls.name: Convert
controls.tooltip:
Changes the body type of the selected object. Converts BRep (solid or surface) faces to a T-Spline face. Converts a T-Spline body to a BRep body. Converts a quad mesh to a T-Spline body.

Select the object to convert.

controls.name: User Coordinate System (UCS)
controls.tooltip:
Creates a custom coordinate system that you can reference in assembly relationships, manufacturing setups or other downstream workflows.

Select a Snap point on a component to place the coordinate system. Optionally, adjust its position, orientation, and axis alignment.

controls.name: Offset Plane
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Plane that is offset from the selected face or plane.

Select a face, plane or sketch profile, then specify the offset distance.

controls.name: Plane at Angle
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Plane through an edge, axis, or line at a specific angle.

Select a linear edge, axis, or sketch line to position the plane, then specify the rotation angle.

controls.name: Tangent Plane
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Plane that is tangent to a face.

Select a face to create a plane tangent to, then select a reference point or face or plane (when cylindrical face is selected) to align to or adjust the angle to rotate the plane around face.

controls.name: Midplane
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Plane at the midpoint between two faces or planes.

Select two faces or planes to create a Construction Plane between them.

controls.name: Perpendicular Plane
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Plane that is perpendicular to a plane or face.

Select a plane or face to create a construction plane that is perpendicular to the plane or face. Optionally, select a point or face to refine location.

controls.name: Plane Through Two Edges
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Plane that passes through two edges or axes.

Select two linear edges, axes or sketch lines to create a Construction Plane through.

controls.name: Plane Through Three Points
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Plane that passes through three points or vertices.

Select three points or vertices to create a Construction Plane through.

controls.name: Plane Along Path
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Plane normal to an edge or sketch line.

Select an edge or sketch line to create a Construction Plane along.

controls.name: Axis Through Cylinder/Cone/Torus
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Axis through the center of a cylinder, cone or torus.

Select a cylinder, cone, or torus to create an axis through its center.

controls.name: Axis Perpendicular To Face
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Axis that is perpendicular to a face and passes through a specific point.

Select a face or plane and a vertex or sketch point to create an axis that is perpendicular to the plane and coincident with the point.

controls.name: Axis Through Two Planes
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Axis coincident with the intersection of two faces or planes.

Select two faces or planes to create an axis where they intersect.

controls.name: Axis Through Two Points
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Axis that passes through two points or vertices.

Select two vertices or sketch points to create a Construction Axis that is coincident with both vertices and points.

controls.name: Axis Through Edge
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Axis along a linear edge or sketch curve.

Select a linear edge, axis or sketch line to place the axis.

controls.name: Point At Vertex
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Point at an existing point or vertex.

Select a vertex or sketch point to place the Construction Point.

controls.name: Point Through Two Edges
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Point at the intersection or extended intersection of two edges.

Select two edges or sketch lines to create a Construction Point where they intersect.

controls.name: Point Through Three Planes
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Point at the intersection or extended intersection of three non-parallel planes or faces.

Select three planes, faces, or sketch profiles to create a Construction Point where they intersect.

controls.name: Point At Center Of Circle/Sphere/Torus
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Point at the center of a circle, sphere, or torus.

Select a circular face or sketch profile, spherical face, or toroidal face to create a Construction Point at its center.

controls.name: Point At Edge And Plane
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Point at the intersection of a linear edge, sketch line, or axis with a face or plane.

Select a linear edge, sketch line, or axis and a face or plane to create a Construction Point where they intersect.

controls.name: Point Along Path
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Point at a specific distance along the path.

Select an edge, sketch line, or curve to use as the path to create the Construction Point along. Optionally, specify a distance to place the point.

controls.name: Measure
controls.tooltip:
Measures the distance, angle, area, or position of selected objects.

Select an object to measure it, and optionally select a second object to measure it and the distance between them.

controls.name: Interference
controls.tooltip:
Reports the interference between selected solid bodies or components.

Select the components then click compute. Choose to create components from the interferences.

controls.name: Section Analysis
controls.tooltip:
Creates a view that cuts through all visible objects in a design to reveal interior details and obscured features.

Select a planar object to define the cut plane, then adjust the distance and angles to position it in the design. In the Browser, the Section Analysis displays in the Analysis folder, where you can adjust its visibility, edit it, or delete it.

controls.name: Curvature Comb Analysis
controls.tooltip:
Displays a comb with sample points along selected edges of a body to help you analyze the curvature of a surface.

Select edges to analyze on a body, then adjust the density and scale of the curvature comb.

controls.name: Curvature Map Analysis
controls.tooltip:
Displays a color gradient on bodies to help you analyze areas of high and low surface curvature.

Select bodies to analyze, then select a curvature map type and adjust the display settings of the curvature map.

controls.name: Draft Analysis
controls.tooltip:
Displays a color gradient on the faces of selected bodies to help evaluate the manufacturability of your design.

Select the bodies to evaluate and the axis to define the direction. Use the options to refine the gradient display.

controls.name: Environment Map Analysis
controls.tooltip:
Applies environment map analysis to selected bodies.

Select bodies, choose an environment, then adjust rotate, opacity, and quality options.

controls.name: Isocurve Analysis
controls.tooltip:
Applies UV mapping and curvature combs to analyze the quality of a surface.

Select bodies or faces to analyze, select the isocurve type, then adjust the number of isocurves to display. You can also display curvature combs and control their density and scale.

controls.name: Validate
controls.tooltip:
Checks the quality of selected surfaces and attempts to heal surfaces before stitching into quilts and solids.

Select the surfaces to check, specify a tolerance then select the type of validation to perform.

controls.name: Zebra Analysis
controls.tooltip:
Displays alternating black and white stripes on a body to help you analyze the curvature of a surface.

Select bodies to analyze, then adjust the direction, repeats, and opacity of the zebra stripes.

controls.name: Accessibility Analysis
controls.tooltip:
Used to colorize an object based on whether or not certain parts of the object are accessible from a particular plane.

Inaccessible areas are highlighted in red. Useful for checking undercut areas through a plane.

controls.name: Center of Mass
controls.tooltip:
Displays a center mark glyph at the center of mass for the selected objects.

You can measure from the center mark to other objects.

controls.name: Minimum Radius Analysis
controls.tooltip:
Displays colors on the model that represent the minimum radius for the curvature of the concave faces.

Detect the minimum fit for holes and fillets. Useful for determining tool sizes in machining.

controls.name: DOF Analysis
controls.tooltip: Displays Degree of Freedom of each component in the Assembly.

controls.name: Fastener Stack Analysis
controls.tooltip:
Displays fastener stacks and their status with respect to engagement settings.

Fastener stacks are recognized based on relative spatial placement of fasteners.

controls.name: Find Similar Components
controls.tooltip: Finds components in your hub that are similar to those in the active design. You can select similar components and open them or insert them into your design. This is available for solid bodies only.

controls.name: Navigator
controls.tooltip:
Shows how data elements connect in a visual graph.

Double click any subassembly node to explore its connected data.

controls.name: Display Component Colors
controls.tooltip:
Displays each component in an assembly as a different color to make them easier to differentiate. Hides physical materials and appearances.

Press Shift+N to show or hide component colors in the canvas. Right-click a component and select Cycle Component Color to change its color.

controls.name: Display Mesh Face Groups
controls.tooltip:
Display face groups on mesh bodies to make them easier to work with. Hides component colors, physical materials and appearances.

Press Shift+F to show or hide mesh face groups

controls.name: Assembly Statistics
controls.tooltip: Displays Assembly Statistics of the Assembly.

controls.name: Change Summary
controls.tooltip:
Displays a list of changes made to the current assembly and its external references.

Select a component to highlight it in the canvas.

controls.name: History
controls.tooltip:
Displays the version history of the selected component.

Select a component to view its version history and optionally choose a different version.

controls.name: Sustainability Insights
controls.tooltip:
Displays an estimated carbon footprint of the current design.

Select a body to analyze, then specify manufacturing details to improve your footprint estimate. You can also activate a persistent dock to monitor selected bodies as you work.

controls.name: Decal
controls.tooltip:
Places an image on a selected face as a cosmetic decal.

Select a PNG, JPG, or TIF image file from a Fusion project or your local computer. Select a face on a solid or surface body to apply it to, then adjust its orientation, scale, and opacity.

controls.name: Canvas
controls.tooltip:
Places an image on a planar face or sketch plane.

Select a face then select an image to import.

controls.name: Insert T-Spline
controls.tooltip:
Inserts a T-Spline Mesh (TSM) file as a single T-Spline body or a T-Spline Scene (TSS) file as one or more T-Spline bodies.

Select the TSM or TSS file you want to insert, then click Open. The T-Spline bodies display in the canvas and Browser and you can use the Form tools to edit them.

controls.name: Insert SVG
controls.tooltip:
Imports an SVG file into the active sketch.

Use SVG files for vector artwork such as logos or custom text.

controls.name: Insert DXF
controls.tooltip:
Inserts geometry from a DXF file into the active sketch.

Select a face or plane, select the DXF file to insert, then position the geometry on the plane.

Select the unit type that matches the units from the original design that generated the DXF.

controls.name: Insert Mesh
controls.tooltip:
Inserts an existing STL, OBJ, or 3MF file as a mesh body into the active component in a design.

Select a file to insert. The contents of the file displays as a mesh body in the canvas and the browser.

For STL or OBJ files, select the unit type that matches the units from the original design that generated the STL or OBJ.

controls.name: Insert Component
controls.tooltip:
Inserts the selected component into the current design.

Select the component to insert then use the manipulator to adjust the position.

controls.name: Insert Fastener
controls.tooltip:
Inserts a fastener into the active document.

Use a combination of searching, filtering and browsing to locate a fastener, adjust the settings, and select a geometry (an edge, a face, a sketch point, an existing fastener) or place a fastener anywhere in the canvas to position it.

controls.name: Duplicate With Joints
controls.tooltip:
Duplicates components in an assembly and the joints attached to them.

Select components to duplicate, select a Joint Origin Mode, then select a Snap point to place each instance. If a component has multiple joints, select the next row in the selection box, then select a Snap point to place each instance.

controls.name: Insert Derive
controls.tooltip:
Pulls and links design features from another design into the active design. When you update the derived features in the original design, the changes are reflected in the destination design.

Before you start, activate the component that you want to contain the derived design features. Select a design, then select a set of components, bodies, sketches, construction geometry, flat patterns, or parameters to derive into the current design.

controls.name: Insert McMaster-Carr Component
controls.tooltip:
Insert a McMaster-Carr Component into the active document.

Browse to the desired component, click the Product Detail CAD icon, select the file type, then click Save.

controls.name: Insert a manufacturer part
controls.tooltip: parts4cad lets you browse and configure millions of parts from more than 400 supplier and manufacturer catalogs and insert them into your designs.

controls.name: Insert TraceParts Supplier Components
controls.tooltip: With TraceParts, boost your design productivity and access millions of CAD models from hundreds of supplier catalogs.

controls.name: Add To Assembly
controls.tooltip:
Inserts the active design into an Assembly Design as an external component.

Select an Assembly Design to insert into, then use the manipulators in the canvas or Initial Position dialog to place the component in the target design.

controls.name: Select
controls.tooltip:
Selection is always active and the active selection mode displays here.

Hold Ctrl (Windows) or Command (MacOS) to add objects to or remove objects from the selection. Change the active selection mode by selecting the mode you want to work with from the menu. Use the selection mode and selection filters to fine tune selection.

controls.name: Window Selection
controls.tooltip:
Selects objects enclosed in a rectangular selection area.

Click and drag from left to right (window selection) to select objects enclosed by the selection boundary. Click and drag from right to left (crossing selection) to select all visible objects the selection boundary intersects and encloses.

Use Selection Filters to include or exclude objects by type.

controls.name: Freeform Selection
controls.tooltip:
Selects objects enclosed in an irregular (lasso) selection area.

A clockwise boundary shape selects all objects within the boundary. A counterclockwise boundary shape selects all visible objects crossed by the boundary.

Use Selection Filters to include or exclude objects by type.

controls.name: Paint Selection
controls.tooltip:
Press and hold the left mouse button and move across objects to select them.

Use Selection Filters to include or exclude objects by type.

children.name: Select By Name
children.tooltip:
Selects bodies or components by the name used in the Browser.

Enter a portion of the object name, check the object types to include, then click Find. You can search using one or more characters or words, finding only objects having that string in the name.

children.name: Select By Boundary
children.tooltip:
Selects objects using a boundary shape you choose.

Select a body to set the centroid, boundary shape, Selection Type, and whether intersected objects are selected.

children.name: Select By Size
children.tooltip:
Selects bodies or components within a size range that you specify.

Use the slider controls or specify the minimum and maximum size values. The size value is the distance between the opposing diagonal corners of the body or component bounding box.

children.name: Invert Selection
children.tooltip:
Switches the selection state of all objects.

Selection is based on the active selection filter and selection mode.

children.name: Seed And Boundary
children.tooltip:
Automatically creates a selection set that includes faces on a solid or surface body that are located between a set of boundary objects and a seed object.

Select faces or edges on a solid or surface body to define the selection boundary, then select a face on the body to use as the seed object for the selection set. Click Update to refresh the selection set based on the current boundary and seed objects.

controls.name: Component Drag
controls.tooltip:
Enables or disables the movement of components by dragging in the canvas.

Hold Alt to drag components when Component Drag is disabled.

children.name: Select Body Priority
children.tooltip:
Sets the selection filter to Bodies, and prevents selection of other object types.

Click a body to select it. Hold Ctrl (Windows) or Command (MacOS) to add objects to or remove objects from the selection. Click Select Body Priority again to restore selection of any object type.

children.name: Select Face Priority
children.tooltip:
Sets the selection filter to Body Faces, and prevents selection of other object types.

Click a face to select it. Hold Ctrl (Windows) or Command (MacOS) to add objects to or remove objects from the selection. Click Select Face Priority again to restore selection of any object type.

children.name: Select Edge Priority
children.tooltip:
Sets the selection filter to Body Edges, and prevents selection of other object types.

Click an edge on a body to select it. Hold Ctrl (Windows) or Command (MacOS) to add objects to or remove objects from the selection. Click Select Edge Priority again to restore selection of any object type.

children.name: Select Component Priority
children.tooltip:
Sets the selection filter to Components, and prevents selection of other object types.

Click a component to select it. Hold Ctrl (Windows) or Command (MacOS) to add objects to or remove objects from the selection. Click Select Component Priority again to restore selection of any object type.

controls.name: Selection Filters
controls.tooltip:
Specifies which object types can be selected.

Use Select All to include or exclude all object types. Check only specific types to limit selection to those types. Check Select Through to enable selection of hidden objects during Window or Freeform selection.

controls.name: Finish Base Feature
controls.tooltip: Return to the Design workspace.

controls.name: New Component
controls.tooltip:
Creates a new internal or external component in the assembly.

Select type and parent, then name the component. For external components, select location. For internal components, you can select bodies to create a component for each.

controls.name: Create Sketch
controls.tooltip:
Enters Sketch mode, where you create geometric profiles that define the foundation of a design. Then use commands like Extrude, Revolve, and Loft to create 3D bodies from sketches.

Select a construction plane, then create lines, arcs, or points to create sketch and construction geometry. Constrain sketches with dimensions and constraints. Select Finish Sketch to exit Sketch mode.

controls.name: Create Form
controls.tooltip:
Enters Form mode and inserts a form feature into the timeline. Use form tools to create and edit history-free bodies by pushing and pulling on vertices, edges, and faces. This is commonly referred to as T-Spline modeling.

Select Finish Form to exit out of the mode.

controls.name: Derive
controls.tooltip:
Pushes and links design features from the active design into a new or existing design. When you update the derived features in the original design, the changes are reflected in the destination design.

Select a single component or a set of components, bodies, sketches, construction geometry, flat patterns, or parameters to derive from the active design.

controls.name: Extrude
controls.tooltip:
Adds depth to open or closed sketch profiles or planar faces.

Select the profile or planar face then specify the distance to extrude.

controls.name: Revolve
controls.tooltip:
Revolves a sketch profile or planar face around a selected axis.

Select a profile or planar face and an axis to revolve around, then specify the extent type, direction, and operation.

controls.name: Sweep
controls.tooltip:
Sweeps a sketch profile or planar face along a selected path.

Select the profile then select the sweep path. The distance for the sweep is a decimal percentage of the selected path.

controls.name: Loft
controls.tooltip:
Creates a smooth shape that transitions between two or more sketch profiles or faces.

Select a series of profiles, planar faces, or non-planar faces to define the shape. Optionally, select rails or centerlines to guide the shape.

controls.name: Patch
controls.tooltip:
Creates a planar or 3D surface within the boundary of a specified closed loop.

Select the loop to patch then apply connected (G0), tangent (G1), and curvature (G2) boundary conditions.

controls.name: Ruled
controls.tooltip:
Creates a ruled surface at a specified distance and angle from selected edges.

Select edges on a solid body, surface body, or sketch. Then select a ruled surface type and specify the direction, distance, and angle.

controls.name: Offset
controls.tooltip:
Creates a new surface body at a given distance from the selected face or surface body.

Select a face or surface body to offset, then specify the distance.

controls.name: Box
controls.tooltip:
Creates a surface body box.

Select a plane, draw a rectangle then specify the height of the box.

controls.name: Cylinder
controls.tooltip:
Creates a surface body cylinder.

Select a plane, draw a circle then specify the height of the cylinder.

controls.name: Sphere
controls.tooltip:
Creates a surface sphere.

Select a plane then specify the center point of the sphere and the diameter.

controls.name: Torus
controls.tooltip:
Creates a surface torus.

Specify the center point and diameter of the axis of revolution of the torus.

controls.name: Coil
controls.tooltip:
Creates a surface coil.

Select a plane then draw a circle to specify the major diameter of the coil. Finish defining the coil using the manipulators or dialog box.

controls.name: Pipe
controls.tooltip:
Creates a surface pipe that follows a selected path.

Select the path then specify the section and size.

children.name: Rectangular Pattern
children.tooltip:
Duplicates faces, bodies, features, or components in a design and distributes them along linear axes in rows and columns to create a rectangular pattern.

Select the object type, then select objects to pattern in the canvas, Browser, or Timeline. Select one or more axes to distribute the pattern instances along, then adjust distribution, quantity, and distance. Check Suppression, then uncheck instances in the canvas to remove them from the pattern.

children.name: Circular Pattern
children.tooltip:
Duplicates faces, bodies, features, or components in a design and distributes them around a linear axis to create a circular pattern.

Select the object type, then select objects to pattern in the canvas, Browser, or Timeline. Select the axis to distribute the pattern instances around, then adjust distribution, quantity, and distance. Check Suppression, then uncheck instances in the canvas to remove them from the pattern.

children.name: Pattern on Path
children.tooltip:
Duplicates faces, bodies, features, or components in a design and distributes them to create a pattern along a specific path.

Select the object type, then select objects to pattern in the canvas, Browser, or Timeline. Select the path to distribute the pattern instances along, then adjust distribution, quantity, and distance. Check Suppression, then uncheck instances in the canvas to remove them from the pattern.

children.name: Geometric Pattern
children.tooltip:
Creates a pattern with size and distribution gradients across a face on a solid body.

Select the face to pattern across, select a solid body as the object to pattern, then adjust the size and distribution settings.

controls.name: Mirror
controls.tooltip:
Creates a copy of selected faces, bodies, features, or components, mirrored across a plane.

Select the objects to mirror, then select the mirror plane.

controls.name: Thicken
controls.tooltip:
Adds thickness to surface faces to create a solid body.

Select the faces to thicken, then specify a thickness value.

controls.name: Boundary Fill
controls.tooltip:
Creates, joins or removes volumes using bounding volumes formed by tool selections.

Select solids, surfaces or workplanes as tools to form volumes (or cells). These cells can be used to cut existing solids or to join to existing solids or to create a new solid.

controls.name: Joint Origin
controls.tooltip:
Positions a joint origin on a component. Joint origins define the geometry used to relate a joint's components.

Select geometry to define the joint origin.

controls.name: Press Pull
controls.tooltip: Modifies the selected geometry using offset, extrude, or fillet commands. The operation depends on the geometry selected.

controls.name: Edit Face
controls.tooltip:
Converts the selected face to T-Spline faces, edges, and vertices for modification.

Select the face to modify. Increase the length and width factors to add faces to give more control.

controls.name: Fillet
controls.tooltip:
Rounds the edges of a solid body by adding material to interior edges and removing material from exterior edges.

Select edges, faces, or features, then specify a radius. Use the Rule Fillet type to add fillets based on specified rules. Use the Full Round Fillet type to round the edges over three adjacent faces.

controls.name: Chamfer
controls.tooltip:
Bevels the edges of a solid or surface body by removing material from exterior edges or adding material to interior edges.

Select edges, faces, or features, then specify one distance, two distances, or a distance and an angle.

controls.name: Trim
controls.tooltip:
Removes the selected area of a surface body using the specified cutting tool.

Select the cutting tool to use then select faces or surface bodies to remove.

controls.name: Untrim
controls.tooltip:
Extends trimmed surfaces and fills gaps, holes, or empty regions.

Select the surface to untrim, then select the untrim type. You can untrim all edges, internal edges, external edges, or manually select the edges you want to untrim.

controls.name: Extend
controls.tooltip:
Enlarges a surface by extending its edges a specified distance.

Select the edges of a surface, select an extension type, then specify the distance to extend. Select an edge alignment option to control the curvature continuity between faces.

controls.name: Stitch
controls.tooltip:
Joins surfaces to make a single surface body or solid body.

Select the surfaces to join. Edges within the tolerance are highlighted green.

controls.name: Unstitch
controls.tooltip:
Breaks joined surfaces into individual surfaces.

Select faces to unstitch. The selected face is unhooked from the parent body and the result body contains the unhooked face.

controls.name: Merge
controls.tooltip:
Combines the selected faces into a single quilt surface.

Select the faces to merge. You can select solid or surface faces.

controls.name: Reverse Normal
controls.tooltip:
Flips the positive direction of all faces on a selected surface body.

Select a surface body to reverse.

controls.name: Scale
controls.tooltip:
Scales sketch objects, bodies, or components.

Select the objects to scale then specify the scale factor.

controls.name: Split Face
controls.tooltip:
Divides faces using a selected profile, face, or plane as the cutting tool.

Select the faces to modify then select the profile, face, or plane that divides the source face.

controls.name: Split Body
controls.tooltip:
Creates new bodies by dividing selected bodies using a profile, face, or plane.

Select the bodies to modify then select the profile, face, or plane that divides the bodies.

controls.name: Move/Copy
controls.tooltip:
Moves the selected face, body, sketch, or construction geometry a specified distance or angle.

Select the objects to modify then specify the distance or angle. Use Set Pivot to reposition the manipulator.

controls.name: Align
controls.tooltip:
Moves an object (component, body, sketch, work geometry) by aligning geometry selected from the object with geometry selected elsewhere. Geometry can be a point, line, plane, circle, or coordinate system. Snaps are treated as full coordinate systems for full position and orientation alignment.

Select the point on the object to move then select the point on the face to align to. Click Flip and Angle to rotate the object.

controls.name: Delete
controls.tooltip:
Permanently deletes selected objects, and everything related to them, from the design. Does not create a feature in the timeline. Deleted objects cannot be restored parametrically.

Select components, bodies, sketches, and construction objects to delete. Use the Remove command to preserve parametric history.

controls.name: Remove
controls.tooltip:
Deletes selected components or bodies from the design and preserves the operation as a feature in the timeline. Removed objects can be restored parametrically.

Select components or bodies to remove. To permanently delete parametric history associated with an object, use the Delete command instead.

controls.name: Convert
controls.tooltip:
Changes the body type of the selected object. Converts BRep (solid or surface) faces to a T-Spline face. Converts a T-Spline body to a BRep body. Converts a quad mesh to a T-Spline body.

Select the object to convert.

controls.name: Physical Material
controls.tooltip:
Assigns physical materials to components and bodies in a design to control their thermal, mechanical, strength, and advanced engineering properties, as well as their appearance.

Drag physical materials onto components or bodies in the canvas or the Browser. In the In This Design section, right-click physical materials to edit, duplicate, delete, or add them as favorites.

controls.name: Appearance
controls.tooltip:
Assigns appearances to components, bodies, or faces in a design to override the color and texture of their physical materials, without affecting physical engineering properties.

Choose whether to apply appearances to components and bodies or specific faces, then drag appearances onto components, bodies, or faces in the canvas or the Browser. In the In This Design section, right-click appearances to edit, duplicate, delete, or add them as favorites.

controls.name: Manage Materials
controls.tooltip:
Opens the Material Browser, where you can manage physical materials and appearances in user-defined material libraries.

Navigate between libraries, create new libraries, and add physical materials or appearances to your Favorites. In custom libraries, edit the properties of physical materials and appearances, or create new ones.

controls.name: Change Parameters
controls.tooltip:
Displays the Parameters dialog, where you can create and manage equations and relationships to control the size of objects.

Edit the name, expression, and comments for parameters. Create User Parameters to use in other expressions.

controls.name: Compute All
controls.tooltip:
Computes all of the parameters, features, and assembly relationships in a design.

Use at major milestones in the design process and after making significant changes to features in the Timeline, to ensure all assembly relationships are calculated properly.

controls.name: Compute Unresolved
controls.tooltip:
Computes only the features related to unresolved external components in the assembly.

Only available when you open a design that contains unresolved external components. You must compute the features related to the unresolved components before you can edit or save the design.

controls.name: User Coordinate System (UCS)
controls.tooltip:
Creates a custom coordinate system that you can reference in assembly relationships, manufacturing setups or other downstream workflows.

Select a Snap point on a component to place the coordinate system. Optionally, adjust its position, orientation, and axis alignment.

controls.name: Offset Plane
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Plane that is offset from the selected face or plane.

Select a face, plane or sketch profile, then specify the offset distance.

controls.name: Plane at Angle
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Plane through an edge, axis, or line at a specific angle.

Select a linear edge, axis, or sketch line to position the plane, then specify the rotation angle.

controls.name: Tangent Plane
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Plane that is tangent to a face.

Select a face to create a plane tangent to, then select a reference point or face or plane (when cylindrical face is selected) to align to or adjust the angle to rotate the plane around face.

controls.name: Midplane
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Plane at the midpoint between two faces or planes.

Select two faces or planes to create a Construction Plane between them.

controls.name: Perpendicular Plane
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Plane that is perpendicular to a plane or face.

Select a plane or face to create a construction plane that is perpendicular to the plane or face. Optionally, select a point or face to refine location.

controls.name: Plane Through Two Edges
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Plane that passes through two edges or axes.

Select two linear edges, axes or sketch lines to create a Construction Plane through.

controls.name: Plane Through Three Points
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Plane that passes through three points or vertices.

Select three points or vertices to create a Construction Plane through.

controls.name: Plane Along Path
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Plane normal to an edge or sketch line.
