Select an edge or sketch line to create a Construction Plane along.

controls.name: Axis Through Cylinder/Cone/Torus
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Axis through the center of a cylinder, cone or torus.

Select a cylinder, cone, or torus to create an axis through its center.

controls.name: Axis Perpendicular To Face
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Axis that is perpendicular to a face and passes through a specific point.

Select a face or plane and a vertex or sketch point to create an axis that is perpendicular to the plane and coincident with the point.

controls.name: Axis Through Two Planes
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Axis coincident with the intersection of two faces or planes.

Select two faces or planes to create an axis where they intersect.

controls.name: Axis Through Two Points
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Axis that passes through two points or vertices.

Select two vertices or sketch points to create a Construction Axis that is coincident with both vertices and points.

controls.name: Axis Through Edge
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Axis along a linear edge or sketch curve.

Select a linear edge, axis or sketch line to place the axis.

controls.name: Point At Vertex
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Point at an existing point or vertex.

Select a vertex or sketch point to place the Construction Point.

controls.name: Point Through Two Edges
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Point at the intersection or extended intersection of two edges.

Select two edges or sketch lines to create a Construction Point where they intersect.

controls.name: Point Through Three Planes
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Point at the intersection or extended intersection of three non-parallel planes or faces.

Select three planes, faces, or sketch profiles to create a Construction Point where they intersect.

controls.name: Point At Center Of Circle/Sphere/Torus
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Point at the center of a circle, sphere, or torus.

Select a circular face or sketch profile, spherical face, or toroidal face to create a Construction Point at its center.

controls.name: Point At Edge And Plane
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Point at the intersection of a linear edge, sketch line, or axis with a face or plane.

Select a linear edge, sketch line, or axis and a face or plane to create a Construction Point where they intersect.

controls.name: Point Along Path
controls.tooltip:
Creates a Construction Point at a specific distance along the path.

Select an edge, sketch line, or curve to use as the path to create the Construction Point along. Optionally, specify a distance to place the point.

controls.name: Measure
controls.tooltip:
Measures the distance, angle, area, or position of selected objects.

Select an object to measure it, and optionally select a second object to measure it and the distance between them.

controls.name: Interference
controls.tooltip:
Reports the interference between selected solid bodies or components.

Select the components then click compute. Choose to create components from the interferences.

controls.name: Section Analysis
controls.tooltip:
Creates a view that cuts through all visible objects in a design to reveal interior details and obscured features.

Select a planar object to define the cut plane, then adjust the distance and angles to position it in the design. In the Browser, the Section Analysis displays in the Analysis folder, where you can adjust its visibility, edit it, or delete it.

controls.name: Curvature Comb Analysis
controls.tooltip:
Displays a comb with sample points along selected edges of a body to help you analyze the curvature of a surface.

Select edges to analyze on a body, then adjust the density and scale of the curvature comb.

controls.name: Curvature Map Analysis
controls.tooltip:
Displays a color gradient on bodies to help you analyze areas of high and low surface curvature.

Select bodies to analyze, then select a curvature map type and adjust the display settings of the curvature map.

controls.name: Draft Analysis
controls.tooltip:
Displays a color gradient on the faces of selected bodies to help evaluate the manufacturability of your design.

Select the bodies to evaluate and the axis to define the direction. Use the options to refine the gradient display.

controls.name: Environment Map Analysis
controls.tooltip:
Applies environment map analysis to selected bodies.

Select bodies, choose an environment, then adjust rotate, opacity, and quality options.

controls.name: Isocurve Analysis
controls.tooltip:
Applies UV mapping and curvature combs to analyze the quality of a surface.

Select bodies or faces to analyze, select the isocurve type, then adjust the number of isocurves to display. You can also display curvature combs and control their density and scale.

controls.name: Validate
controls.tooltip:
Checks the quality of selected surfaces and attempts to heal surfaces before stitching into quilts and solids.

Select the surfaces to check, specify a tolerance then select the type of validation to perform.

controls.name: Zebra Analysis
controls.tooltip:
Displays alternating black and white stripes on a body to help you analyze the curvature of a surface.

Select bodies to analyze, then adjust the direction, repeats, and opacity of the zebra stripes.

controls.name: Accessibility Analysis
controls.tooltip:
Used to colorize an object based on whether or not certain parts of the object are accessible from a particular plane.

Inaccessible areas are highlighted in red. Useful for checking undercut areas through a plane.

controls.name: Center of Mass
controls.tooltip:
Displays a center mark glyph at the center of mass for the selected objects.

You can measure from the center mark to other objects.

controls.name: Minimum Radius Analysis
controls.tooltip:
Displays colors on the model that represent the minimum radius for the curvature of the concave faces.

Detect the minimum fit for holes and fillets. Useful for determining tool sizes in machining.

controls.name: DOF Analysis
controls.tooltip: Displays Degree of Freedom of each component in the Assembly.

controls.name: Fastener Stack Analysis
controls.tooltip:
Displays fastener stacks and their status with respect to engagement settings.

Fastener stacks are recognized based on relative spatial placement of fasteners.

controls.name: Find Similar Components
controls.tooltip: Finds components in your hub that are similar to those in the active design. You can select similar components and open them or insert them into your design. This is available for solid bodies only.

controls.name: Navigator
controls.tooltip:
Shows how data elements connect in a visual graph.

Double click any subassembly node to explore its connected data.

controls.name: Display Component Colors
controls.tooltip:
Displays each component in an assembly as a different color to make them easier to differentiate. Hides physical materials and appearances.

Press Shift+N to show or hide component colors in the canvas. Right-click a component and select Cycle Component Color to change its color.

controls.name: Display Mesh Face Groups
controls.tooltip:
Display face groups on mesh bodies to make them easier to work with. Hides component colors, physical materials and appearances.

Press Shift+F to show or hide mesh face groups

controls.name: Assembly Statistics
controls.tooltip: Displays Assembly Statistics of the Assembly.

controls.name: Change Summary
controls.tooltip:
Displays a list of changes made to the current assembly and its external references.

Select a component to highlight it in the canvas.

controls.name: History
controls.tooltip:
Displays the version history of the selected component.

Select a component to view its version history and optionally choose a different version.

controls.name: Sustainability Insights
controls.tooltip:
Displays an estimated carbon footprint of the current design.

Select a body to analyze, then specify manufacturing details to improve your footprint estimate. You can also activate a persistent dock to monitor selected bodies as you work.

controls.name: Decal
controls.tooltip:
Places an image on a selected face as a cosmetic decal.

Select a PNG, JPG, or TIF image file from a Fusion project or your local computer. Select a face on a solid or surface body to apply it to, then adjust its orientation, scale, and opacity.

controls.name: Canvas
controls.tooltip:
Places an image on a planar face or sketch plane.

Select a face then select an image to import.

controls.name: Insert T-Spline
controls.tooltip:
Inserts a T-Spline Mesh (TSM) file as a single T-Spline body or a T-Spline Scene (TSS) file as one or more T-Spline bodies.

Select the TSM or TSS file you want to insert, then click Open. The T-Spline bodies display in the canvas and Browser and you can use the Form tools to edit them.

controls.name: Insert SVG
controls.tooltip:
Imports an SVG file into the active sketch.

Use SVG files for vector artwork such as logos or custom text.

controls.name: Insert DXF
controls.tooltip:
Inserts geometry from a DXF file into the active sketch.

Select a face or plane, select the DXF file to insert, then position the geometry on the plane.

Select the unit type that matches the units from the original design that generated the DXF.

controls.name: Insert Mesh
controls.tooltip:
Inserts an existing STL, OBJ, or 3MF file as a mesh body into the active component in a design.

Select a file to insert. The contents of the file displays as a mesh body in the canvas and the browser.

For STL or OBJ files, select the unit type that matches the units from the original design that generated the STL or OBJ.

controls.name: Insert Component
controls.tooltip:
Inserts the selected component into the current design.

Select the component to insert then use the manipulator to adjust the position.

controls.name: Insert Fastener
controls.tooltip:
Inserts a fastener into the active document.

Use a combination of searching, filtering and browsing to locate a fastener, adjust the settings, and select a geometry (an edge, a face, a sketch point, an existing fastener) or place a fastener anywhere in the canvas to position it.

controls.name: Duplicate With Joints
controls.tooltip:
Duplicates components in an assembly and the joints attached to them.

Select components to duplicate, select a Joint Origin Mode, then select a Snap point to place each instance. If a component has multiple joints, select the next row in the selection box, then select a Snap point to place each instance.

controls.name: Insert Derive
controls.tooltip:
Pulls and links design features from another design into the active design. When you update the derived features in the original design, the changes are reflected in the destination design.

Before you start, activate the component that you want to contain the derived design features. Select a design, then select a set of components, bodies, sketches, construction geometry, flat patterns, or parameters to derive into the current design.

controls.name: Insert McMaster-Carr Component
controls.tooltip:
Insert a McMaster-Carr Component into the active document.

Browse to the desired component, click the Product Detail CAD icon, select the file type, then click Save.

controls.name: Insert a manufacturer part
controls.tooltip: parts4cad lets you browse and configure millions of parts from more than 400 supplier and manufacturer catalogs and insert them into your designs.

controls.name: Insert TraceParts Supplier Components
controls.tooltip: With TraceParts, boost your design productivity and access millions of CAD models from hundreds of supplier catalogs.

controls.name: Add To Assembly
controls.tooltip:
Inserts the active design into an Assembly Design as an external component.

Select an Assembly Design to insert into, then use the manipulators in the canvas or Initial Position dialog to place the component in the target design.

controls.name: Select
controls.tooltip:
Selection is always active and the active selection mode displays here.

Hold Ctrl (Windows) or Command (MacOS) to add objects to or remove objects from the selection. Change the active selection mode by selecting the mode you want to work with from the menu. Use the selection mode and selection filters to fine tune selection.

controls.name: Window Selection
controls.tooltip:
Selects objects enclosed in a rectangular selection area.

Click and drag from left to right (window selection) to select objects enclosed by the selection boundary. Click and drag from right to left (crossing selection) to select all visible objects the selection boundary intersects and encloses.

Use Selection Filters to include or exclude objects by type.

controls.name: Freeform Selection
controls.tooltip:
Selects objects enclosed in an irregular (lasso) selection area.

A clockwise boundary shape selects all objects within the boundary. A counterclockwise boundary shape selects all visible objects crossed by the boundary.

Use Selection Filters to include or exclude objects by type.

controls.name: Paint Selection
controls.tooltip:
Press and hold the left mouse button and move across objects to select them.

Use Selection Filters to include or exclude objects by type.

children.name: Select By Name
children.tooltip:
Selects bodies or components by the name used in the Browser.

Enter a portion of the object name, check the object types to include, then click Find. You can search using one or more characters or words, finding only objects having that string in the name.

children.name: Select By Boundary
children.tooltip:
Selects objects using a boundary shape you choose.

Select a body to set the centroid, boundary shape, Selection Type, and whether intersected objects are selected.

children.name: Select By Size
children.tooltip:
Selects bodies or components within a size range that you specify.

Use the slider controls or specify the minimum and maximum size values. The size value is the distance between the opposing diagonal corners of the body or component bounding box.

children.name: Invert Selection
children.tooltip:
Switches the selection state of all objects.

Selection is based on the active selection filter and selection mode.

children.name: Seed And Boundary
children.tooltip:
Automatically creates a selection set that includes faces on a solid or surface body that are located between a set of boundary objects and a seed object.

Select faces or edges on a solid or surface body to define the selection boundary, then select a face on the body to use as the seed object for the selection set. Click Update to refresh the selection set based on the current boundary and seed objects.

controls.name: Component Drag
controls.tooltip:
Enables or disables the movement of components by dragging in the canvas.

Hold Alt to drag components when Component Drag is disabled.

children.name: Select Body Priority
children.tooltip:
Sets the selection filter to Bodies, and prevents selection of other object types.

Click a body to select it. Hold Ctrl (Windows) or Command (MacOS) to add objects to or remove objects from the selection. Click Select Body Priority again to restore selection of any object type.

children.name: Select Face Priority
children.tooltip:
Sets the selection filter to Body Faces, and prevents selection of other object types.

Click a face to select it. Hold Ctrl (Windows) or Command (MacOS) to add objects to or remove objects from the selection. Click Select Face Priority again to restore selection of any object type.

children.name: Select Edge Priority
children.tooltip:
Sets the selection filter to Body Edges, and prevents selection of other object types.

Click an edge on a body to select it. Hold Ctrl (Windows) or Command (MacOS) to add objects to or remove objects from the selection. Click Select Edge Priority again to restore selection of any object type.

children.name: Select Component Priority
children.tooltip:
Sets the selection filter to Components, and prevents selection of other object types.

Click a component to select it. Hold Ctrl (Windows) or Command (MacOS) to add objects to or remove objects from the selection. Click Select Component Priority again to restore selection of any object type.

controls.name: Selection Filters
controls.tooltip:
Specifies which object types can be selected.

Use Select All to include or exclude all object types. Check only specific types to limit selection to those types. Check Select Through to enable selection of hidden objects during Window or Freeform selection.

controls.name: Finish Base Feature
controls.tooltip: Return to the Design workspace.

controls.name: Line
controls.tooltip:
Creates lines and arcs.

Select a start and endpoint to define a line segment. Click and drag the endpoint of a segment to define an arc.

controls.name: Midpoint Line
controls.tooltip:
Creates a line that is symmetrical from the midpoint.

Specify the midpoint to start a line, and click to set the end of the line.

children.name: 2-Point Rectangle
children.tooltip:
Creates a rectangle using two points for the diagonal corners.

Select the first point as the start of the rectangle. Select the second point or specify the width and height values.

children.name: 3-Point Rectangle
children.tooltip:
Creates a rectangle using three points to define width, direction, and height.

Select the first point as the start of the rectangle. Select a second point or specify a distance value and pick a point. Select a third point or specify a distance value.

children.name: Center Rectangle
children.tooltip:
Creates a rectangle using two points to define the center and one corner.

Select the first point as the center of the rectangle. Select a corner point or specify width and height values.

children.name: Center Diameter Circle
children.tooltip:
Creates a circle using a center point and diameter.

Select to define the center point then specify the diameter.

children.name: 2-Point Circle
children.tooltip:
Creates a circle defined by two points.

Specify two points on the diameter of the circle.

children.name: 3-Point Circle
children.tooltip:
Creates a circle defined by three points.

Specify three points on the circumference of the circle. The points define the size and position of the circle.

children.name: 2-Tangent Circle
children.tooltip:
Creates a circle tangent to two sketch lines.

Select two lines then specify the radius of the circle.

children.name: 3-Tangent Circle
children.tooltip:
Creates a circle tangent to three sketch lines.

Select three lines that the circle will be tangent to.

children.name: 3-Point Arc
children.tooltip:
Creates an arc using three points.

Select the start point, end point, and then a point on the arc.

children.name: Center Point Arc
children.tooltip:
Creates an arc using three points.

Select the center point, then select start point and last select the end point or specify an angle value.

children.name: Tangent Arc
children.tooltip:
Creates an arc with tangency.

Select two points.

children.name: Circumscribed Polygon
children.tooltip:
Creates a polygon using the center point and the midpoint of one edge.

Select the center point of the polygon. Specify a value for the number of sides. Select the midpoint of an edge or specify a distance and select a point.

children.name: Inscribed Polygon
children.tooltip:
Creates a polygon using the center point and a vertex.

Select the center point of the polygon. Specify a value for the number of edges. Select a vertex point or specify a distance and select a point.

children.name: Edge Polygon
children.tooltip:
Creates a polygon by defining a single edge and the position of the polygon.

Select the start and end points of one edge or select the start point then specify a distance and angle. Specify the number of sides. Select a point to define the orientation of the polygon.

controls.name: Ellipse
controls.tooltip:
Creates an ellipse defined by a center point, major axis and a point on the ellipse.

Select the center point of the ellipse. Select the second point to define the first axis. Select the third point to define a point on the ellipse.

children.name: Center to Center Slot
children.tooltip:
Creates a linear slot defined by placement and distance of slot arc centers, and by slot width.

Specify centers of both slot arcs. Click to specify slot width, or enter diameter of the slot arcs.

children.name: Overall Slot
children.tooltip:
Creates a linear slot defined by orientation, length and width.

Specify the start and end on the slot center line. Click to specify slot width, or enter diameter of the slot arcs.

children.name: Center Point Slot
children.tooltip:
Creates a linear slot defined by a center point, location of slot arc centers, and by slot width.

Specify the slot center, and place center of a slot arc. Click to specify slot width, or enter diameter of the slot arcs.

children.name: Three Point Arc Slot
children.tooltip:
Creates an arc slot defined by a three point center arc and slot width.

Specify the start and end point of the slot center arc. Specify the third point of the center arc, or enter center arc radius. Click to specify slot width, or enter diameter or radius of the slot arcs.

children.name: Center Point Arc Slot
children.tooltip:
Creates an arc slot defined by a center point, two point center arc and slot width.

Specify the center point of the slot. Specify the start and end point of the slot center arc. Click to specify slot width or enter diameter or radius of the slot arc.

children.name: Fit Point Spline
children.tooltip:
Creates a spline through the selected fit points.

Select the first point to start the spline. Select additional points as fit points.

children.name: Control Point Spline
children.tooltip:
Creates a spline driven by the selected control points.

Select the first point to start the spline. Select additional points as control points.

children.name: Control Point Spline
children.tooltip:
Creates a spline driven by the selected control points.

Select the first point to start the spline. Select additional points as control points.

controls.name: Conic Curve
controls.tooltip:
Creates a curve driven by endpoints and Rho value. Depending on the Rho value, the curve can be elliptical, parabolic, or hyperbolic.

Select the start point, end point, and then the top of the vertex. Use the guidelines to create a tangency constraint. Specify the Rho value for the desired shape of the conic curve.

controls.name: Point
controls.tooltip:
Creates an individual sketch point to use as reference geometry.

Click in the canvas to create a point. You can snap to the grid or existing geometry. Use sketch points to define construction geometry, position hole features, space points on a spline, or connect lines in 3D space.

controls.name: Text
controls.tooltip:
Creates text inside a rectangular frame or along a selected path, which you can use as a profile to create 3D geometry.

Place the text frame or select the path for text to follow, then enter and format your text.

controls.name: Mirror
controls.tooltip:
Mirrors the selected sketch curves about a selected sketch line.

Select the curves to mirror then select the line to mirror about.

controls.name: Circular Pattern
controls.tooltip:
Duplicates selected sketch curves in an arc or circular pattern.

Select the curves to pattern, the point to revolve around, and the quantity.

controls.name: Rectangular Pattern
controls.tooltip:
Duplicates sketch curves in rows and columns.

Select the curves to pattern then specify the direction, quantity, and distance.

children.name: Project
children.tooltip:
Projects the body silhouette, edges, work geometries and sketch curves into the active sketch plane.

Use the selection filter to project specific type of geometry or the body silhouette.

children.name: Intersect
children.tooltip:
Projects the points, model edges, work geometries, and sketch curves that intersect the active sketch plane.

Use the selection filter to project specific type of geometry or the entire model.

children.name: Spun Profile
children.tooltip:
Rotates selected geometry around a specified axis and projects a 2D spun profile on to the active sketch plane.

Use the selection filter to project specific geometry types or the body silhouette.

children.name: Include 3D Geometry
children.tooltip:
Include edges, work geometry, and sketch curves into the current sketch.

Select the objects to include.

children.name: Project To Surface
children.tooltip: Project sketch geometry, edge, vertex, or workpoint to selected faces.

children.name: Intersection Curve
children.tooltip:
Creates a 3D sketch curve from intersecting geometry.

The first selection is the sketch curve. The second selection is the sketch curve or faces to intersect with. You can select multiple curves or faces to intersect with.

children.name: Isoparametric Curve
children.tooltip:
Creates smooth curves along a face in the U or V direction.

Select to create a single curve or a series of curves, select a face, and specify the curve distribution on the face.

controls.name: Sketch Dimension
controls.tooltip:
Create sketch dimensions for sketch geometries. Use dimensions to control the size or position of sketch objects.

Select the sketch curves to dimension then select an area to position the dimension.

controls.name: Fillet
controls.tooltip:
Places an arc of a specified radius at the intersection of two lines or arcs.

Select the vertex or the two lines or arcs. Specify a radius for the fillet.

children.name: Equal Distance Chamfer
children.tooltip:
Creates a chamfer at the vertex, intersection, or apparent intersection of two lines in a sketch, based on an equal distance to each side.

Select a vertex or two lines, then specify the distance value for the chamfer.

children.name: Distance and Angle Chamfer
children.tooltip:
Creates a chamfer at the vertex, intersection, or apparent intersection of two lines in a sketch, based on a single distance and an angle.

Select a vertex or two lines, then specify the distance and angle values for the chamfer.

children.name: Two Distance Chamfer
children.tooltip:
Creates a chamfer at the vertex, intersection, or apparent intersection of two lines in a sketch, based on a different distance to each side.

Select a vertex or two lines, then specify the two distance values for the chamfer.

controls.name: Blend Curve
controls.tooltip:
Creates a tangent or curvature continuous blend curve between the endpoints of two sketch curves or edges.

Select two sketch curves or edges in the canvas to blend.

controls.name: Offset
controls.tooltip:
Copies the selected sketch curves a specified distance from the original curves.

Select the curves to offset then specify the offset distance.

controls.name: Trim
controls.tooltip:
Trims a sketch curve to the nearest intersecting curve or boundary geometry.

Pause the cursor over the curve to preview the portion to be trimmed. Select the curve to trim.

controls.name: Extend
controls.tooltip:
Extends a curve to the nearest intersecting curve or boundary geometry.

Pause the cursor over the curve to preview the portion to be extended. Select the curve to extend it.

controls.name: Break
controls.tooltip:
Breaks a sketch entity into two or more segments where it intersects other sketch entities.

Pause the cursor over the sketch entity to preview where it will be broken, then click to break it.

controls.name: Sketch Scale
controls.tooltip:
Scales sketch geometry.

Select sketch geometry to scale, select the point from which to scale, then drag the manipulator handle in the canvas or specify an exact Scale Factor value.

controls.name: Move/Copy
controls.tooltip:
Moves the selected face, body, sketch, or construction geometry a specified distance or angle.

Select the objects to modify then specify the distance or angle. Use Set Pivot to reposition the manipulator.

controls.name: Change Parameters
controls.tooltip:
Displays the Parameters dialog, where you can create and manage equations and relationships to control the size of objects.

Edit the name, expression, and comments for parameters. Create User Parameters to use in other expressions.

controls.name: AutoConstrain
controls.tooltip: Generates options using AI technology to automatically dimension and constrain your sketch. Review the proposals and select the one that best suits your needs.

controls.name: AutoConstrain from datum
controls.tooltip: Place a datum point to align the constraints and dimensions to, then AI technology automatically generates options with dimension and constraints added your sketch. Review the proposals and select the one that best suits your needs.

controls.name: Horizontal/Vertical
controls.tooltip: Constrains a single line, or two points, to lie on either the vertical or horizontal axis, whichever is closer to the current alignment.

controls.name: Coincident
controls.tooltip:
Constrains the position of two points or a point and a line or curve together.

This could be a point constrained along a line, two points constrainted to each other, or a point constrained along a curve.

controls.name: Tangent
controls.tooltip: Constrains a curve and another object so that they touch at a single point but never cross each other.

controls.name: Equal
controls.tooltip: Constrains similar objects so that their sizes are identical. When the size of one object changes, the others adjust, too.

controls.name: Parallel
controls.tooltip: Constrains two lines so that they extend in the same direction and never intersect.

controls.name: Perpendicular
controls.tooltip: Constrains two objects so that they lie perpendicular (at a 90-degree angle) to each other.

controls.name: Fix/UnFix
controls.tooltip: Locks the size and location of a point or object.

controls.name: MidPoint
controls.tooltip: Constrains a point or object to the midpoint of another object.

controls.name: Concentric
controls.tooltip: Constrains two or more arcs, circles, or ellipses to the same center point.

controls.name: Collinear
controls.tooltip:
Constrains two or more objects so that they share a common line.

This could be a line and a rectangle, where the line and one edge of the rectangle lie along the same line.

controls.name: Symmetry
controls.tooltip: Constrains two or more objects so that they are symmetrical (identical to each other in relation to a common axis).

controls.name: Curvature
controls.tooltip: Constrains two or more objects to create a smooth, continuous curvature between them (G2 continuity).

controls.name: Polygon
controls.tooltip: Constrains a closed sketch profile with sides of the same length and equal angles as a regular polygon.

controls.name: Configure
controls.tooltip:
Opens the Configuration Table, enters Configuration Mode, and highlights configurable features and objects in the Timeline and Browser.

Add Configurations as rows in the table to create different variants of a design. Click highlighted features and objects to add their configurable aspects as columns in the table.

controls.name: Display Configuration Table
controls.tooltip: Shows or hides the Configure dialog without entering Configuration Mode.

controls.name: Create Configuration Rules
controls.tooltip:
Creates logical Configuration Rules that drive or limit configured aspect values in a Configured Design, to ensure only valid configurations can be created.

Drag and drop blocks into the Configuration Rules canvas to create logical rules, then apply them to the set of configurations.

controls.name: Measure
controls.tooltip:
Measures the distance, angle, area, or position of selected objects.

Select an object to measure it, and optionally select a second object to measure it and the distance between them.

controls.name: Interference
controls.tooltip:
Reports the interference between selected solid bodies or components.

Select the components then click compute. Choose to create components from the interferences.

controls.name: Section Analysis
controls.tooltip:
Creates a view that cuts through all visible objects in a design to reveal interior details and obscured features.

Select a planar object to define the cut plane, then adjust the distance and angles to position it in the design. In the Browser, the Section Analysis displays in the Analysis folder, where you can adjust its visibility, edit it, or delete it.

controls.name: Curvature Comb Analysis
controls.tooltip:
Displays a comb with sample points along selected edges of a body to help you analyze the curvature of a surface.

Select edges to analyze on a body, then adjust the density and scale of the curvature comb.

controls.name: Environment Map Analysis

controls.name: Canvas
controls.tooltip:
Places an image on a planar face or sketch plane.

Select a face then select an image to import.

controls.name: Insert T-Spline
controls.tooltip:
Inserts a T-Spline Mesh (TSM) file as a single T-Spline body or a T-Spline Scene (TSS) file as one or more T-Spline bodies.

Select the TSM or TSS file you want to insert, then click Open. The T-Spline bodies display in the canvas and Browser and you can use the Form tools to edit them.

controls.name: Insert SVG
controls.tooltip:
Imports an SVG file into the active sketch.

Use SVG files for vector artwork such as logos or custom text.

controls.name: Insert DXF
controls.tooltip:
Inserts geometry from a DXF file into the active sketch.

Select a face or plane, select the DXF file to insert, then position the geometry on the plane.

Select the unit type that matches the units from the original design that generated the DXF.

controls.name: Insert Mesh
controls.tooltip:
Inserts an existing STL, OBJ, or 3MF file as a mesh body into the active component in a design.

Select a file to insert. The contents of the file displays as a mesh body in the canvas and the browser.

For STL or OBJ files, select the unit type that matches the units from the original design that generated the STL or OBJ.

controls.name: Insert Component
controls.tooltip:
Inserts the selected component into the current design.

Select the component to insert then use the manipulator to adjust the position.

controls.name: Insert Fastener
controls.tooltip:
Inserts a fastener into the active document.

Use a combination of searching, filtering and browsing to locate a fastener, adjust the settings, and select a geometry (an edge, a face, a sketch point, an existing fastener) or place a fastener anywhere in the canvas to position it.

controls.name: Duplicate With Joints
controls.tooltip:
Duplicates components in an assembly and the joints attached to them.

Select components to duplicate, select a Joint Origin Mode, then select a Snap point to place each instance. If a component has multiple joints, select the next row in the selection box, then select a Snap point to place each instance.

controls.name: Insert Derive
controls.tooltip:
Pulls and links design features from another design into the active design. When you update the derived features in the original design, the changes are reflected in the destination design.

Before you start, activate the component that you want to contain the derived design features. Select a design, then select a set of components, bodies, sketches, construction geometry, flat patterns, or parameters to derive into the current design.

controls.name: Insert McMaster-Carr Component
controls.tooltip:
Insert a McMaster-Carr Component into the active document.

Browse to the desired component, click the Product Detail CAD icon, select the file type, then click Save.

controls.name: Insert a manufacturer part
controls.tooltip: parts4cad lets you browse and configure millions of parts from more than 400 supplier and manufacturer catalogs and insert them into your designs.

controls.name: Insert TraceParts Supplier Components
controls.tooltip: With TraceParts, boost your design productivity and access millions of CAD models from hundreds of supplier catalogs.

controls.name: Add To Assembly
controls.tooltip:
Inserts the active design into an Assembly Design as an external component.

Select an Assembly Design to insert into, then use the manipulators in the canvas or Initial Position dialog to place the component in the target design.

controls.name: Select
controls.tooltip:
Selection is always active and the active selection mode displays here.

Hold Ctrl (Windows) or Command (MacOS) to add objects to or remove objects from the selection. Change the active selection mode by selecting the mode you want to work with from the menu. Use the selection mode and selection filters to fine tune selection.

controls.name: Window Selection
controls.tooltip:
Selects objects enclosed in a rectangular selection area.

Click and drag from left to right (window selection) to select objects enclosed by the selection boundary. Click and drag from right to left (crossing selection) to select all visible objects the selection boundary intersects and encloses.

Use Selection Filters to include or exclude objects by type.

controls.name: Freeform Selection
controls.tooltip:
Selects objects enclosed in an irregular (lasso) selection area.

A clockwise boundary shape selects all objects within the boundary. A counterclockwise boundary shape selects all visible objects crossed by the boundary.

Use Selection Filters to include or exclude objects by type.

controls.name: Paint Selection
controls.tooltip:
Press and hold the left mouse button and move across objects to select them.

Use Selection Filters to include or exclude objects by type.

children.name: Select By Name
children.tooltip:
Selects bodies or components by the name used in the Browser.

Enter a portion of the object name, check the object types to include, then click Find. You can search using one or more characters or words, finding only objects having that string in the name.

children.name: Select By Boundary
children.tooltip:
Selects objects using a boundary shape you choose.

Select a body to set the centroid, boundary shape, Selection Type, and whether intersected objects are selected.

children.name: Select By Size
children.tooltip:
Selects bodies or components within a size range that you specify.

Use the slider controls or specify the minimum and maximum size values. The size value is the distance between the opposing diagonal corners of the body or component bounding box.

children.name: Invert Selection
children.tooltip:
Switches the selection state of all objects.

Selection is based on the active selection filter and selection mode.

children.name: Seed And Boundary
children.tooltip:
Automatically creates a selection set that includes faces on a solid or surface body that are located between a set of boundary objects and a seed object.

Select faces or edges on a solid or surface body to define the selection boundary, then select a face on the body to use as the seed object for the selection set. Click Update to refresh the selection set based on the current boundary and seed objects.

controls.name: Component Drag
controls.tooltip:
Enables or disables the movement of components by dragging in the canvas.

Hold Alt to drag components when Component Drag is disabled.

children.name: Select Body Priority
children.tooltip:
Sets the selection filter to Bodies, and prevents selection of other object types.

Click a body to select it. Hold Ctrl (Windows) or Command (MacOS) to add objects to or remove objects from the selection. Click Select Body Priority again to restore selection of any object type.

children.name: Select Face Priority
children.tooltip:
Sets the selection filter to Body Faces, and prevents selection of other object types.

Click a face to select it. Hold Ctrl (Windows) or Command (MacOS) to add objects to or remove objects from the selection. Click Select Face Priority again to restore selection of any object type.

children.name: Select Edge Priority
children.tooltip:
Sets the selection filter to Body Edges, and prevents selection of other object types.

Click an edge on a body to select it. Hold Ctrl (Windows) or Command (MacOS) to add objects to or remove objects from the selection. Click Select Edge Priority again to restore selection of any object type.

children.name: Select Component Priority
children.tooltip:
Sets the selection filter to Components, and prevents selection of other object types.

Click a component to select it. Hold Ctrl (Windows) or Command (MacOS) to add objects to or remove objects from the selection. Click Select Component Priority again to restore selection of any object type.

controls.name: Selection Filters
controls.tooltip:
Specifies which object types can be selected.

Use Select All to include or exclude all object types. Check only specific types to limit selection to those types. Check Select Through to enable selection of hidden objects during Window or Freeform selection.

controls.name: Finish Sketch
controls.tooltip: Exits the edit sketch state.

controls.name: Finish with AutoConstrain
controls.tooltip:
No sketches to constrain.

Add a sketch and then run this tool to automatically generate options to dimension and constrain your sketch.

controls.name: Press Pull
controls.tooltip: Modifies the selected geometry using offset, extrude, or fillet commands. The operation depends on the geometry selected.

controls.name: Edit Face
controls.tooltip:
Converts the selected face to T-Spline faces, edges, and vertices for modification.

Select the face to modify. Increase the length and width factors to add faces to give more control.

controls.name: Fillet
controls.tooltip:
Rounds the edges of a solid body by adding material to interior edges and removing material from exterior edges.

Select edges, faces, or features, then specify a radius. Use the Rule Fillet type to add fillets based on specified rules. Use the Full Round Fillet type to round the edges over three adjacent faces.

controls.name: Chamfer
controls.tooltip:
Bevels the edges of a solid or surface body by removing material from exterior edges or adding material to interior edges.

Select edges, faces, or features, then specify one distance, two distances, or a distance and an angle.

controls.name: Shell
controls.tooltip:
Offsets the walls of a solid body to create a hollow cavity with walls of a specified thickness.

Select a body to shell or faces to remove to create an opening, then specify a type, direction, and wall thickness.

controls.name: Draft
controls.tooltip:
Applies a fixed or parting line draft angle to planar faces.

Select a pull direction, parting tool, and faces to draft, then specify the draft angle.

controls.name: Scale
controls.tooltip:
Scales sketch objects, bodies, or components.

Select the objects to scale then specify the scale factor.

controls.name: Combine
controls.tooltip:
Joins, cuts, or intersects two or more solid bodies to create a single solid body.

Select the target body, select one or more tool bodies to combine with the target body, then select the operation to use to combine the bodies together.

controls.name: Replace Face
controls.tooltip:
Replaces one or more part faces with different face. The new face must completely intersect the part.

Select the face to remove then select the new face.

controls.name: Split Face
controls.tooltip:
Divides faces using a selected profile, face, or plane as the cutting tool.

Select the faces to modify then select the profile, face, or plane that divides the source face.

controls.name: Split Body
controls.tooltip:
Creates new bodies by dividing selected bodies using a profile, face, or plane.

Select the bodies to modify then select the profile, face, or plane that divides the bodies.

controls.name: Silhouette Split
controls.tooltip:
Splits a body using surfaces generated from its silhouette curves.

Set the view direction by selecting a plane or axis then select the body and choose a split operation.

controls.name: Move/Copy
controls.tooltip:
Moves the selected face, body, sketch, or construction geometry a specified distance or angle.

Select the objects to modify then specify the distance or angle. Use Set Pivot to reposition the manipulator.

controls.name: Align
controls.tooltip:
Moves an object (component, body, sketch, work geometry) by aligning geometry selected from the object with geometry selected elsewhere. Geometry can be a point, line, plane, circle, or coordinate system. Snaps are treated as full coordinate systems for full position and orientation alignment.

Select the point on the object to move then select the point on the face to align to. Click Flip and Angle to rotate the object.

controls.name: Delete
controls.tooltip:
Permanently deletes selected objects, and everything related to them, from the design. Does not create a feature in the timeline. Deleted objects cannot be restored parametrically.

Select components, bodies, sketches, and construction objects to delete. Use the Remove command to preserve parametric history.

controls.name: Change Parameters
controls.tooltip:
Displays the Parameters dialog, where you can create and manage equations and relationships to control the size of objects.

Edit the name, expression, and comments for parameters. Create User Parameters to use in other expressions.

controls.name: Compute All
controls.tooltip:
Computes all of the parameters, features, and assembly relationships in a design.

Use at major milestones in the design process and after making significant changes to features in the Timeline, to ensure all assembly relationships are calculated properly.

controls.name: Compute Unresolved
controls.tooltip:
Computes only the features related to unresolved external components in the assembly.

Only available when you open a design that contains unresolved external components. You must compute the features related to the unresolved components before you can edit or save the design.

controls.name: Convert
controls.tooltip:
Changes the body type of the selected object. Converts BRep (solid or surface) faces to a T-Spline face. Converts a T-Spline body to a BRep body. Converts a quad mesh to a T-Spline body.

Select the object to convert.

controls.name: Measure
controls.tooltip:
Measures the distance, angle, area, or position of selected objects.

Select an object to measure it, and optionally select a second object to measure it and the distance between them.

controls.name: Interference
controls.tooltip:
Reports the interference between selected solid bodies or components.

Select the components then click compute. Choose to create components from the interferences.

controls.name: Section Analysis
controls.tooltip:
Creates a view that cuts through all visible objects in a design to reveal interior details and obscured features.

Select a planar object to define the cut plane, then adjust the distance and angles to position it in the design. In the Browser, the Section Analysis displays in the Analysis folder, where you can adjust its visibility, edit it, or delete it.

children.tooltip:

children.tooltip:

controls.tooltip:

For STL or OBJ files, select the unit type that matches the units from the original design that generated the STL or OBJ.

controls.name: Repair
controls.tooltip:
Repairs a mesh body to prepare it for further design and manufacturing operations.

Select a mesh body to repair, then select a repair type. For the Rebuild repair type, select a rebuild type, then adjust density and offset.

controls.name: Generate Face Groups
controls.tooltip:
Automatically generates face groups on a mesh body using the normal angles between faces to determine the boundaries of each face group.

To display face groups, toggle Inspect > Display Mesh Face Groups. Select mesh bodies or face groups, select the generation method, then adjust the face opening angle, tolerance, and minimal area ratio.

controls.name: Combine Face Groups
controls.tooltip:
Combines two or more adjacent face groups on a mesh body.

To display face groups, toggle Inspect > Display Mesh Face Groups. Select two or more adjacent face groups on the mesh body to combine them.

controls.name: Create Face Group
controls.tooltip:
Creates a face group from a selection of faces on a mesh body.

To display face groups, toggle Inspect > Display Mesh Face Groups. Select faces on a mesh body to include in the face group. Adjust the settings in the Mesh Selection Palette to refine the selection set.

controls.name: Direct Edit
controls.tooltip:
Creates a mesh base feature that you can edit directly.

Select the mesh body to edit. A mesh base feature displays on the timeline and you can make local modifications to the mesh body without capturing the changes in the parametric history of the design.

controls.name: Remesh
controls.tooltip:
Refines or coarsens faces on a mesh body or face groups.

Select a mesh body or face groups on a mesh body, then adjust the settings to regenerate the mesh faces.

controls.name: Reduce
controls.tooltip:
Reduces the number of faces on a mesh body to minimize complexity.

Select a mesh body or face groups, select a reduction target, then adjust the settings to reduce the number of mesh faces.

controls.name: Plane Cut
controls.tooltip:
Uses a plane to trim or split a mesh body.

Select a mesh body, then select and position the cutting plane. The cut can trim the body, split the body into multiple bodies, or split the faces only. For the Trim and Split Body cut types, select a fill type to generate watertight bodies.

controls.name: Shell
controls.tooltip:
Hollows the interior of a mesh body.

Select a mesh body, then adjust the direction and thickness to hollow the interior volume.

controls.name: Combine
controls.tooltip:
Joins, intersects, cuts, or merges two or more mesh bodies to create a single mesh body.

Select the target body, select one or more tool bodies to combine with the target body, then select the operation to use to combine the bodies together.

controls.name: Smooth
controls.tooltip:
Smooths rough or creased regions on a mesh body.

Select a mesh body or face groups, select a smoothing type, then adjust the smoothness and scale to smooth rough or creased regions.

controls.name: Smooth Boundary
controls.tooltip:
Smooths the boundary edges of a mesh body.

Select a mesh body or face groups to smooth the boundary edges, improving mesh quality near open boundaries.

controls.name: Reverse Normal
controls.tooltip:
Reverses the normal direction of selected faces on a mesh body.

Select faces on a mesh body to reverse their normal direction.

controls.name: Close Cracks
controls.tooltip:
Closes small cracks and gaps in a mesh body.

Select a mesh body to close cracks and seal small gaps between triangles.

controls.name: Erase And Fill
controls.tooltip:
Removes and replaces faces on a mesh body to fill holes and repair regions.

Select the boundary of faces around a hole to fill, or select the faces of a region to remove and replace.

controls.name: Bridge
controls.tooltip:
Bridges two regions of a mesh body by creating connecting geometry between them.

Select two face groups or sets of faces on a mesh body, then adjust the density to bridge them together.

controls.name: Mesh Align
controls.tooltip:
Aligns a face on a mesh body to a plane with one transformation.

Select a mesh face, then select a plane to align the body to.

controls.name: Attract to Reference
controls.tooltip:
Attracts selected faces on a mesh body towards a reference mesh body.

Select faces on a mesh body to edit, select a reference mesh body, then adjust density, smoothness, and offset to control the attraction.

controls.name: Texture Extrude
controls.tooltip:
Uses an image to add surface texture to a mesh body.

Select faces, face groups, or a mesh body to add texture to and choose an image to use for the texture. Specify the extrude type and distance then adjust the image scale and placement.

Optionally, repeat the texture in a grid pattern across the selected geometry.

controls.name: Separate
controls.tooltip:
Separates regions of a mesh body into independent mesh bodies.

Select a separation type, then select a mesh body or face groups to separate into individual bodies.

Select the objects to modify then specify the distance or angle. Use Set Pivot to reposition the manipulator.

controls.name: Scale Mesh

Scales mesh bodies from a reference point.

Select mesh bodies, select a reference point to scale from and a scale type, then specify the scale factor to scale the mesh bodies.
